Jensen Huang’s return as CEO to Nvidia hasn’t eased the scrutiny the company confronts. The chipmaker still faces multiple inquiries into allegations that its advanced GPUs were smuggled into China by a customer, the Singapore-based data center operator Megaspeed, in violation of US export rules designed to slow China’s development of frontier AI models.
The central question for investigators is what Nvidia knew about where those chips ended up, and whether Huang’s affair with a Megaspeed executive gave the company reason to doubt Megaspeed’s assurances. Huang’s return doesn’t settle that. US Attorney General Todd Blanche has suggested Nvidia isn’t a target of an investigation, but California’s attorney general and Congress are pressing ahead, and the Securities & Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating, too.
The US government opened an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 and requested information from Nvidia about its billions of dollars in sales to the company, concerned that some of the chips Megaspeed bought for data center projects in Malaysia were in fact being diverted to China. Singapore also began investigating similar allegations in 2025. Megaspeed has denied any wrongdoing.
Diversion of this kind would be a fairly routine issue for a company like Nvidia, whose in-demand chips are the targets of smugglers and re-sellers. When it comes to compliance and liability for export control violations, Nvidia and other chip sellers need assurances that the end users of their chips are obeying the rules. However, they also cannot ignore other information that might call the reliability of those assurances into question, export control attorneys told TechCrunch.
And that’s why Jensen Huang’s affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang was such a problem for Nvidia, likely even more so than her alleged role as a source for Chinese intelligence agencies. If Nvidia personnel, from lower-level employees up to the CEO, had reason to believe that statements from Megaspeed weren’t reliable, the attorneys said, that would increase the company’s legal risk.
“Government investigators likely would want to know, notwithstanding whatever formal assurances were exchanged between the parties, what anyone at Nvidia actually knew about the end use and end users of the chips,” Dan Fisher-Owens, an attorney at the firm Berliner Corcoran & Rowe, told TechCrunch last week.
The concern Nvidia’s board faced when it decided to oust Huang is that he knew more about what Megaspeed was doing with Nvidia’s products than was reflected in any of the compliance statements. The Wall Street Journal reported that Alice Huang and her husband, Kang Wei, were part of a network of businesses that funneled chips to a company in Shanghai. Kang also reportedly introduced his wife to Jensen Huang, whom he had known for a decade.
On Monday, the US government added Megaspeed and its affiliates to a list of companies restricted from US trade due to national security concerns. The US also issued new rules last week barring large data centers that purchase US chips from serving customers in China and other nations seen as problematic by the US government. Nvidia, meanwhile, said it would stop selling licensed chips to China, and laid out plans to hire its first compliance officer and create a new board committee focused on export controls.
Nvidia’s board said it reinstated Huang on Monday after receiving “input from senior levels of the United States government” that left it confident his return posed no national security risk. President Donald Trump later said he called into the meeting to give them that assurance.
In a news conference Tuesday, Blanche said that Nvidia was “a good corporate citizen” and suggested it is not the target of an investigation, but Blanche declined to answer questions about the government’s investigation into Megaspeed, which the Justice Department said was ongoing as recently as last week.
“When you say the export investigation is still ongoing, I don’t know what you’re talking about,” Blanche said.
Other authorities may be more demanding. Nvidia faces investigations by California Attorney General Rob Bonta and, reportedly , the SEC, both tied to its corporate disclosures. While many details of the investigation still aren’t known, short sellers complained about the company’s decision to stop breaking out its exports to Singapore in financial filings after journalists raised concerns about chip diversion.
Members of Congress from both parties say they want answers from Nvidia, with many citing alarm about China and some questioning the White House’s role in Huang’s return. Three committees in the House of Representatives will privately interview Huang and Nvidia’s top lawyer, Tim Teter, next week. Teter reportedly intervened in the Department of Commerce’s investigation of Megaspeed last year.
“We remain committed to getting answers on the mass smuggling of Nvidia products, their diversion for Chinese military purposes, and their key role in advancing our foremost adversary’s AI capabilities,” the Republican chairs of House committees focused on foreign affairs, intelligence, and China said in a joint statement.
Rep. Brian Mast, the chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, has also demanded that the Department of Commerce share extensive data regarding its investigation into chip smuggling, including by Megaspeed and its affiliates.
The Senate Banking Committee will also question Huang in a public hearing on Dec. 3.
“Mr. Huang, Nvidia executives, and the company’s board still owe Congress answers about the company’s compliance with U.S. export controls,” Senator Elizabeth Warren, the ranking Democratic member on the committee, said in a statement. “The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what ‘input’ was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement.”

Trump boosts Nvidia boss return but are US politicians on board?
After the AI chipmaker Nvidia announced it was bringing back embattled former head Jensen Huang and the company's stock shot up like a bullet, President Donald Trump took a very public victory lap.
"I made the deal," he said during a lengthy phone interview with cable business news channel CNBC.
Trump followed that with an AI-generated image posted to his social media platform that riffed on the famous photograph taken moments after the 2024 attempt on his life in Pennsylvania. But instead of Trump in the image, Huang was the one surrounded by Secret Service guards. It depicted him in front of an Nvidia banner - with a raised fist clenching a red bra.
The post was classic Trump – potentially offensive, yet still a bit opaque.
Was Trump suggesting Huang survived a scandal – one that includes allegations of recklessly jeopardising US national security by consorting with a suspected Chinese spy – the way he had survived an assassin's bullet?
Was the bra a celebration Huang's reported extramarital affairs? By replacing the US flag with an Nvidia standard, was he claiming that America and one of its largest, most powerful companies are one and the same?
At the very least, the image underscores how inextricably linked Huang and Trump now are, with the fate of the former hinging on the successes and failures of the latter.
And with that comes significant risks for the American president and for Republicans, including Vice-President JD Vance, who played a key part in his efforts to rescue Huang.
While Trump has said that a "very thorough investigation" by federal officials "exonerated" Huang and his reinstatement poses no national security threat, that is far from the final word on the matter.
"Every time you have a Chinese woman that's good looking or beautiful, they say she's a spy," Trump told CNBC, adding that "with Jensen, I don't believe that's true".
Democrats and some concerned Republicans in Congress have a different view.
They are promising to launch their own oversight of Huang and Nvidia, with subpoenas and compelled witness testimony, in order to assess whether they violated laws by allowing China to access sophisticated microchip technology.
State governments could also launch their own investigations.
Any new revelations could further damage the company's standing – and, by association, Trump himself.
"I have warned the administration from the start about Communist China obtaining our most advanced chips through both smuggling and remote access," Republican Senator Tom Cotton posted on X.
US attorney general dodges questions about Nvidia investigation
While Huang has a long record of success at Nvidia, there is no guarantee that he can recapture past glory now that his star his dimmed.
Even if he is free from any criminal liability, the tech mogul is about to be in a much harsher spotlight than he has ever experienced.
Trump also appears to be on the wrong side of public opinion when it comes to AI writ large.
In the recent US midterm elections, candidates on both the left and right campaigned on imposing new restrictions on data centre construction, with many calling for new legal guardrails to prevent AI-fuelled economic and social disruption.
"Rather than addressing the American people's growing concerns about AI, this administration remains asleep at the wheel or willfully ignorant as our most advanced technologies fall into the hands of our greatest competitors," congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove, a California Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, told the BBC.
The president's own political base is also suspicious of the new technology, with rural conservatives often rebelling at the demands that big tech companies have placed on their local resources and civic infrastructure.
The Nvidia story has also exposed rifts in Trump's own administration, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, a China hawk, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, a vocal proponent of AI, publicly feuding over whether to impose new restrictions on AI chip exports.
Both Bessent and Lutnick travelled with Trump on his recent trip to China, although it was the commerce secretary who hitched a ride back to the White House on the Marine One helicopter when Trump returned to Washington last Thursday.
Polling also indicated that political corruption was a top issue for voters this year.
The president's willingness to intervene in the deliberations of a major private company in which he owns millions of dollars of stock could further fuel those concerns.
Trump's decision to help save Huang – noting on Monday that "we have to protect our geniuses, and he certainly is a genius" – could further inflame the public's sense that the rich and powerful, genius or not, play by a different set of rules.
"It almost feels like they've bent the rule, the regulation, to allow this to happen because it's such an important part of our economy right now," Steve Bannon, a former top Trump adviser, said on his podcast on Monday.
"Even in the crash of 2008... I never saw the government step in and take over a board of directors."
For this American president, however, these risks appear to be worth taking because of the stakes involved.
Trump has long viewed the success of the US economy as a key part of his political legacy.
He boasted of the historic growth and low unemployment during his first presidential term (while glossing over the disruptions caused by the Covid pandemic).
And since returning to office, he has celebrated as major US stock indices posted new record highs.
Recent US economic expansion has been fuelled largely by investment in AI technology, and Trump has become one of the industry's biggest boosters.
He scolded states and local governments for blocking data centre construction and predicted that the nation that wins the race for supremacy in AI – which he has tried to rebrand as "super intelligence" – will control the fate of the world.
If Trump views the economy as the key to his political success and AI as instrumental to the health of the US economy, then his dramatic, precedent-shattering actions to try to rescue Nvidia, the company at the centre of America's AI industry, make more sense.
In the weeks since concerns over Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy first surfaced, Nvidia's stock price tumbled more than 32%.
US stock indices tumbled as well, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq down 10% last week and the larger S&P 500 dropping 8.6%.
The recent financial turmoil may have given Trump a glimpse into a future where AI growth is just the latest financial bubble – like the housing market in 2008 and internet companies in 2001 – that is due for a resounding pop, with similarly dire economic consequences to follow.
Trump's intervention on behalf of Huang arrested that drop, at least for a day.
On Tuesday, Nvidia's stock price gave back much of the bounce it had enjoyed, and larger stock indices were mixed. The fate of the America economy and the AI juggernaut that has powered it is still undetermined.
Trump's intervention may not be a crisis fully averted, but only a crisis delayed.
And if an AI reckoning does come, the US president will be hard-pressed to avoid being caught in the maelstrom.

Hunter Schafer first came across Blade Runner when the 2017 sequel was released
"What does it mean to be human?" is a question that's always been at the heart of Blade Runner.
The first film in the series, released in 1982, depicted a technologically advanced yet dystopian version of Los Angeles in the then-distant future of 2019.
While the movie's flying cars haven't - quite - materialised yet in the real world, Blade Runner's themes of technological progress and the threats it poses feel just as relevant.
At least that's what the cast and crew of Blade Runner 2099, a new TV series set in the same universe, are hoping.
BBC Newsbeat spoke to stars Hunter Schafer, Lewis Gribben and Dimitri Abold, plus showrunner Silka Luisa, to ask why they think themes of artificial consciousness and existential threats still resonate.
The original Blade Runner, directed by Sir Ridley Scott, is considered a sci-fi classic that had a long-lasting influence on the genre.
It told the story of Detective Deckard, played by Harrison Ford, who hunted down synthetic humans known as replicants.
Schafer says her first exposure to the series was actually marketing for Blade Runner 2049 - the film sequel starring Ford and Ryan Gosling in 2017.
"I never thought I'd have the opportunity to make an addition to the world," she says.
"And so when that opportunity came along, I was quite thrilled."
Blade Runner 2099 is set 80 years after the original film, and portrays a Los Angeles where replicants have taken over.
Schafer plays Cora, a fugitive human forced to team up with replicant Olwen (played by Michelle Yeoh), as she tries to track down an artefact that could save humanity.
Schafer stars alongside Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh in the new TV adaptation
The series lands at a time when there are disagreements about the nature of the threat AI could pose to humans .
"I think it's particularly relevant right now, especially for the youth and young people who are inheriting a world that's asking a lot of the same questions that the show asks," says Schafer.
"I think that's timely and hopefully helpful to some degree."
But Blade Runner 2099 isn't "necessarily about just AI", says showrunner Luisa.
"It's this bigger question of what is the world going to be in 15 years and how can you plan for it?" she says.
The first Blade Runner also touched on themes of corporate greed and environmental damage, which are evident in the new series.
Luisa hopes the theme of a future that "is not going to be what you were promised" resonates with viewers today.
"The idea that you were born into a world and you thought you were expecting certain aspects of your life just to roll out," she says.
"That system is collapsing. And so what will be your place in whatever comes next?"
Blade Runner 2049 won awards and scored well with reviewers, but reports suggested it didn't hit box office targets.
This was partly blamed on marketing for the film trying to appeal more to existing fans than new ones - so what would the cast say to get younger viewers on board?
"It's just a very rich world," says Gribben, who plays Cora's younger brother Elias.
Gribben also points out that Blade Runner 2099, which employed "hundreds of artists and craftspeople" according to its makers, is a celebration of traditional film-making despite its themes.
"And I think studios will rely more on technology to make better-looking movies, but they won't have that soul."
Abold, who plays Cora's human ally Bebeto, says one of the show's key messages is about "the connections that you make".
"And the connections that you make are the foundation of humanity," he says.
"Because at the end of the day, all we have is ourselves and each other, right? And that's what feeds any human emotional experience."
Cora is helped by human allies including her brother Elias (Lewis Gribben) and Bebeto (Dimitri Abold)
Reviews for Blade Runner 2099 have been mostly positive, with a score of 72% on Rotten Tomatoes , external and an average of 65% on review aggregator Metacritic , external .
There was praise for the lead performances, the show's visual style and the way it updates the themes established in previous series entries.
The most common criticism was the show's pacing, with several critics describing it as a slow-burn and questioning whether Blade Runner worked as well off the big screen.
Schafer says she felt a lot of pressure when she signed up for the show,
"It's something that we were all aware of when making this show," she says.
"Most people who love film-making love Blade Runner, everybody brought their best to work.
Blade Runner 2099 is available on Prime Video from 25 November.
Listen to Newsbeat live at 12:45 and 17:45 weekdays - or listen back here .

Israel’s tech sector and economy have strong ties to chip giant Nvidia, which invests billions of dollars.
When Jensen Huang returned to lead the chip giant Nvidia this week after a scandal over his extramarital affairs, US President Donald Trump was not the only head of government to welcome his second coming.
Thousands of kilometres away, Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was celebrating too.
Huang once called Israel Nvidia’s “second home”, and Netanyahu reflected that feeling as he wrote on X: “Nvidia’s partnership with Israel’s tech sector has created enormous value for the company and for Israel’s innovation economy.”
“Continuity in Nvidia’s leadership is good news for that partnership and for the global AI industry,” Netanyahu added, referring to Huang’s reinstatement as CEO and president on Monday.
Global headlines have focused on Huang’s affairs, including with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset; his resignation’s implications for the AI industry; and the larger technology race between Washington and Beijing. His reinstatement at the company he cofounded has gone a long way to settle market jitters. Nvidia’s share price rocketed up by 30 percent on Monday.
But Huang’s return has also calmed nerves in Israel – arguably the country most impacted by Nvidia’s performance outside the United States as it hosts the US-based company’s largest overseas operations.
California-based Nvidia, the world’s most valuable semiconductor company with a market capitalisation of about $4 trillion, holds the key to the modern artificial intelligence revolution. Huang’s company holds an extraordinary near-90 percent share of the global market for GPUs – graphics processing units, which are specialised AI processors used in AI data centres.
Nvidia’s operations in Israel are its largest in research and development outside the US. It has doubled employees there in the past three years to 6,000 people across seven research and development centres in Yokne’am, Tel Aviv, Jerusalem, Ra’anana and Beersheba. It also has plans to build a major research and development campus in Kiryat Tivon near Haifa to accommodate up to 10,000 employees.
The Bank of Israel has estimated that Nvidia’s work in the country alone will add 2.2 percentage points of growth to Israel’s gross domestic product (GDP) in 2026, bringing it to 5.6 percent. Without Nvidia, that would be 3.4 percent growth, or 40 percent lower.
Next year, Nvidia is expected to add a further 2.4 percentage points to its GDP growth.
Nvidia paid about $1.29bn in taxes to Israel in its financial year that ended in January, according to its annual report. The company is projected to account for nearly 3 percent of Israel’s total state tax revenues in 2026, according to some estimates.
Huang’s resignation on November 12 initially rattled investors on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE) with the benchmark indices sliding after the announcement.
But by the end of the day, they had recovered. The TA-35 index finished 0.22 per cent higher at the close of the day while the broader TA-125 gained 0.07 per cent. The BlueTech Global Index, which tracks technology companies, fell 0.15 per cent.
The Haaretz newspaper reported, however, that officials at Israel’s Ministry of Finance were concerned about the potential consequences for the Israeli economy of turmoil – and particularly Huang’s exit – at Nvidia.
On Monday, Israeli President Isaac Herzog congratulated Huang on his return, noting “his deep appreciation to Huang for his continued support for Israel and for his commitment to strengthening the connection between Nvidia and Israel”.
Herzog’s office said Huang told the president that he was “moved by the message and that he intends to make the most of the second chance he has been given”.
Nvidia is helping fuel Israel’s economic machine during its genocidal war on Gaza, pogroms by Israeli settlers against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank and the occupation of southern Lebanon.
But Israel is also returning strong numbers for the company.
The root of the tech giant’s relationship with the country can be traced back to Nvidia’s acquisition of Mellanox, an Israeli company that supplies computer networking products, in April 2020 for nearly $7bn. That acquisition was central to Nvidia’s success.
Nvidia was already able to make powerful engines that process AI workloads, but a single GPU cannot handle that workload and needs to exchange information with other GPUs.
Mellanox made the networking infrastructure that allows those engines to work together at a fast pace, creating the foundational structure of a data centre.
Nvidia’s networking business, built around Mellanox, generated more than $21bn in revenues in the third quarter of 2026. That’s about 18 percent of Nvidia’s total quarterly revenue.
At the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas in January, Huang spoke about Israel’s role in the development of key Nvidia chips.
“Nvidia’s BlueField-4 DPU and three networking components – the ConnectX-9 SuperNIC, NVLink 6 Switch and Spectrum-6 Ethernet Switch – all came out of Israel. So four out of six chips came out of Israel,” he said, praising the employees in Israel.
“Pretty amazing and maybe next time, six out of six chips,” Huang added.
A review by the American Friends Service Committee, a group that won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1947 partly for its work rescuing and providing relief to Jews during the Holocaust, has found that the Israeli military uses multiple Nvidia products.
Several purchases of Nvidia products were disclosed by the Israeli Ministry of Defence during Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, a report by the group last year noted.
“They include products that are designed for AI applications, like Jetson cards and DGX,” it said, adding that since the public database only records unclassified contracts, “this likely represents only part of the full scale of the military’s usage of Nvidia products and services.”
Israel has made extensive use of AI systems in the Gaza war – including those known as The Gospel, Lavender and Where’s Daddy? – to track and target Palestinians at an unprecedented scale, the group said, adding that Nvidia “could therefore be potentially implicated in these war crimes”.
The Nvidia Jetson TX2 AI processor is also reportedly integrated into Elbit Systems’ Lanius drones, which Israel has used to kill Palestinian civilians in Gaza.

Silka Luisa explains how she imagined a new iteration of the iconic franchise, and why trench coats are so important.
As a longtime fan of the films, Blade Runner 2099 showrunner Silka Luisa says she was more excited than scared when it came to adapting the series for TV. The new show is set 50 years after the 2017 film Blade Runner 2049 and imagines a bleak future where artificial humans known as replicants have taken over society after a brutal war. Luisa, who previously served as showrunner on Apple TV’s Shining Girls adaptation , says she largely had to put any concerns about the monumental task of following up Blade Runner out of her mind while working on the show.
“I just don’t think you can approach Blade Runner with fear,” she tells The Verge . “It’s a bold concept. It always has been. P.K. Dick took really big swings and it’s not for the timid. So any fears I had I just ignored and kept focused on the monumental task at hand.”
And yet, there was one particular moment during production that made Luisa pause and think about just how big of a deal this project was. Blade Runner 2099 stars Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer as pair of noir detectives — Yeoh is a replicant approaching the end of her life, while Schafer is trying to hide the fact that she’s human — and, in the grand tradition of previous leads Harrison Ford and Ryan Gosling, each has a distinct and iconic jacket. “Once they put the coats on, it really did just transform them,” Luisa says. “The screen test was one of the few moments where I stopped myself and was just blown away by the fact that I was making Blade Runner .”
Blade Runner 2099 is streaming on Amazon Prime Video today, and you can read my chat with Luisa exploring everything from the show’s origins to the research process to those all-important jackets.
What do you think it is about Blade Runner that has made it so enduring?
It’s one of the rare properties that asks really deep philosophical questions, but within a detective noir narrative. I think it’s the juxtaposition of both a structure that’s accessible and familiar, but then these really heady, vital questions: What does it mean to be human? How do you find connection? Just these evergreen concepts that every generation needs to grapple with in their own way and in their own time. There really isn’t anything else like Blade Runner .
Given all of that, was it intimidating or scary to take this on?
I know it seems insane almost to say no, but I just don’t think you can approach Blade Runner with fear. It’s a bold concept. It always has been. P.K. Dick took really big swings and it’s not for the timid. So any fears I had I just ignored and kept focused on the monumental task at hand. And you just stay so concentrated on moving the show forward at each step that you’re not really thinking of it in that objective sense.
Does the time gap in the narrative help with that and give you the space to create your own thing?
Absolutely. Every iteration has evolved forward. [Original Blade Runner director Ridley Scott] took a big leap from the book. There definitely are touchstones from the novel in his film, but he put his own stamp on that story. And [ Blade Runner 2049 director Denis Villeneuve], it’s the same thing. 2049 is mesmerizing, it’s spectacular, but in its own way. It feels like it sits in the world of the Blade Runner canon, but is not a replica of what Ridley did. And that’s what makes it so special. That actually gave us a lot of freedom to try and carve our own path, because if the world is too familiar, it’s not unsettling and it’s not going to give you any feeling of awe. You’ve already seen it before. And so you have to make it your own in some sense.
So where did you start with this story? What was the initial concept?
The starting point was the idea of technology overtaking us. The war between “robots” and humans is something that has been visited in science fiction many times. And to me what felt fresh wasn’t necessarily what the war looked like, but what the aftermath looked like. I couldn’t close my eyes and picture off the top of my head what would happen to us, what would society shift into, what is post-human. That was really exciting. So it definitely started with the concept of this junction point between the world as we know it and a possible world to come.
Was the idea of having this inverse relationship from the original film, where replicants are now hunting humans, always part of the concept?
Yes, it started with the idea of flipping the world, and once you do that at the macro level, you start to think about what is the more intimate story you’re telling. And if you flip the world now suddenly you have a replicant society, it’s not about a replicant trying to look human, it’s the opposite way around. And so an undercover story just seemed like a natural answer to what would be the narrative shape. It also gave me a relationship as opposed to a single person’s journey.
Was it a lot of work imagining what this new replicant society would be like?
So much of the initial writing process was just the visuals. It was really hard to write in spaces that I couldn’t picture. We started to put images up in the writers room from the real world, a blend of films, unusual references from the real world, historical references. You have to ask: What does the texture of the space feel like? Who works there? How long has it existed? What neighborhood is it in? You start to ask all of these questions, and you need to know the answers to write the scenes. It definitely slows the process of writing. Because normally I love to do a lot of historical research. If I’m setting something in a place, I would read a lot about it, and find all of the details in the real world. Here I needed that same amount of detail, but we had to create it.
The Blade Runner films have such a slow and deliberate pacing. How do you think about that when you’re doing a story that’s eight hours long compared to a much shorter movie?
The pacing of the show was one of the biggest conversation points early on, because everybody would be wary of having a truly Blade Runner pace. When you’re in a theater, it is such a meditative experience to be in that world. And there was a fear that if you translate it to television, people won’t have the patience for that. So on the page, I really was pushing the momentum of the storytelling, to the point of even not having exteriors, where you’re just jumping into scenes.
In the editing process, once we started to actually look at cuts, if you cut it too tightly you don’t have these moments of breath where the music can live. Once we had [composer Leopold Ross’] score, and we started putting it to pictures, you want to give him a moment in the sun. You want to have those dreamier sections of the show that are, to me, really fundamental to what makes something Blade Runner . It’s always a question of how far you can stretch the rubber band. Everyone will debate whether the pacing is too slow or too fast, and it’s a really hard calibration.
Blade Runner has such a strong lineage of cool jackets. How important was it to get that look right for both Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer?
Our costume designer Helen [Huang] is phenomenal. Her jackets are incredible, and I love that both of them have really distinct silhouettes. Helen is so thoughtful in how she starts to conceive of these really iconic pieces. For Michelle, she wanted to have something that was referencing a more traditional trench, and then for Hunter it was more of a bomber jacket. She pulled all of these incredible historical references and then blended them with different textures that would make sense with the harsh environment. It’s just masterful work.
Once they put the coats on, it really did just transform them. The screen test was one of the few moments where I stopped myself and was just blown away by the fact that I was making Blade Runner .

Task management app Todoist said on Tuesday that a hacker gained access to its production systems and stole customer data, including email IDs, password hashes, and account creation dates. The company said around 6% of its customers were affected and blamed stolen credentials for the breach.
Todoist said the attacker used stolen credentials to access the company’s version control system and source code between November 22 and 23. The hacker then changed employee access controls and reached the app’s cloud infrastructure via an employee’s work account.
The hacker downloaded credentials of early Todoist users whose passwords were stored using an older hashing method, but didn’t change any source code, the company said. Todoist said it has blocked the attack path and reset passwords as a mitigation step, as well as disabled the Todoist for Outlook email add-on.
For a small number of people, about 0.001% of its userbase, the hacker also searched through tasks, comments and attachment names to look for credentials for other services, like API keys and access tokens.
The hacker also pulled Todoist API tokens and Slack integration tokens, and looked for emails, addresses, and attachment file names through the Todoist for Outlook extension if it was connected to accounts and had permission to read emails.
The company said it has sent a notice to those affected and asked them to reset their credentials and change their login details in other places with the same password. The company is asking users to also update API tokens, reconnect integrations, and revoke or replace any access keys, recovery phrases or credentials they had stored in Todoist comments.
Todoist said it has also reset its internal access structure and how remote command execution works in its cloud environment to prevent such incidents in the future.
Todoist’s founder and CEO, Amir Salihefendić, apologized to users about the incident on X , and said the company will take a closer look at why it happened.
The to-do app’s data breach is the latest in a burgeoning list of data breaches in which hackers use stolen credentials to access data and systems at enterprises. So far this year, we’ve seen several companies fall victim to this form of attack, including Uber and Klue .

Dünya teknoloji devi Nvidia’nın kurucusu ve CEO’su Jensen Huang, 12 Kasım’da patlak veren yasak aşk ve casusluk iddialarının ardından yönetim kurulunun baskısıyla görevinden istifa etmek zorunda kalmıştı. Skandalın merkezinde, Huang’ın yasak aşk yaşadığını kabul ettiği Çinli iş kadını Alice Huang yer alıyordu.
ABD istihbarat yetkililerine göre Alice Huang, ilişki yaşadığı bir yılı aşkın süre boyunca Çin’in en üst düzey casusluk teşkilatından bir yetkiliyle düzenli temas halindeydi. Dahası, kadının çalıştığı Singapur merkezli Megaspeed adlı şirket, ABD’nin ihracat kısıtlamalarını delerek Çin’e gelişmiş Nvidia çipleri kaçırdığı iddiasıyla ABD Adalet Bakanlığı tarafından soruşturuluyordu.
Küresel çapta yankı uyandıran bu krizin ardından Nvidia yönetim kurulu, Huang’ı görevden uzaklaştırmış ve şirkete geri dönmesinin kesinlikle söz konusu olmadığını açıkça ilan etmişti.
Ancak istifanın üzerinden henüz kısacık bir süre geçmişken, Washington ve Silikon Vadisi’ni şaşkına çeviren bir gelişme yaşandı. Geçen hafta sonu Çin ziyaretinden dönen ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Huang’ın istifasının da tetiklediği piyasa düşüşlerini ve borsadaki trilyonlarca dolarlık erimeyi görünce doğrudan müdahale etmeye karar verdi.
Nvidia’da kişisel olarak en az 12 milyon dolarlık hissesi bulunan ve şirketi 21. yüzyıl ekonomisinin temel taşlarından biri olarak gören Trump, bir "dahi" olarak nitelendirdiği Huang’ın koltuğuna geri dönmesi için düğmeye bastı.
Trump bu hassas operasyonu yürütmesi için, Silikon Vadisi ile çok yakın ilişkileri bulunan Başkan Yardımcısı JD Vance’i görevlendirdi. Vance, hafta sonu boyunca hem Jensen Huang hem de Nvidia yönetim kurulu ile son derece gizli görüşmeler yürüttü.
Yönetim kurulunun Huang’ı geri alabilmesi için iki kritik güvenceye ihtiyacı vardı: Birincisi, Huang’ın ulusal güvenlik tehdidi oluşturmadığına dair resmi bir teminat; ikincisi ise hakkında herhangi bir cezai suçlama bulunmadığına dair hukuki bir güvence.
Trump, bu kararı almadan önce Başsavcı Todd Blanche ve Ulusal İstihbarat Direktörü Jay Clayton ile görüştüğünü, Huang’ın çip kaçakçılığında doğrudan bir rolü olmadığından emin olduğunu belirtti.
Hükümetin ve Nvidia’nın en üst düzeyindeki çok dar bir çevrenin haberdar olduğu pazarlıklar pazar gecesi sonuçlandı. Pazartesi sabahı önce Nvidia yönetim kurulu, ardından Donald Trump koordineli açıklamalar yaparak Jensen Huang’ın CEO’luk görevine iade edildiğini duyurdu.
Trump sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada, ABD hükümetinin Huang’ın dönüşünü ulusal güvenlik riski olarak görmediğini ve elinde yasa dışı bir eyleme karıştığına dair hiçbir kanıt bulunmadığını ilan etti. Nvidia yönetimi de hükümetten gelen bu güvencelere dayanarak Huang’ın dönüşünü onayladı; ancak Çin’e çip kaçakçılığı iddiaları nedeniyle şirkete bir ‘baş uyum görevlisi’ atanacağını ve iç soruşturmanın devam edeceğini duyurdu. Bu açıklamaların ardından borsalar hızla yükselirken, Nvidia yatırımcıları tek günde yaklaşık 1 trilyon dolarlık değer kazandı.
Trump’ın kendi istihbarat teşkilatlarının uyarılarını göz ardı ederek özel bir şirketin yönetimine bu denli müdahale etmesi, Washington’da hem Demokratların hem de Cumhuriyetçilerin sert tepkisine yol açtı. Dışişleri Bakanı Marco Rubio da dahil olmak üzere danışmanları tarafından konuyla ilgili en az iki kez bilgilendirilmesine rağmen Trump, istihbarat raporlarına şüpheyle yaklaştığını açıkça dile getirdi.
Çin ziyaretinde Devlet Başkanı Şi Cinping ile bu konuyu bir şikâyet olarak değil, Huang için yaşanan bir "trajedi" olarak konuştuğunu belirten Trump, basına verdiği demeçlerde "Ne zaman güzel bir Çinli kadın görseler casus diyorlar, ama Jensen konusunda buna inanmıyorum" ifadelerini kullandı. Huang’ın eşi Lori ile aralarındaki sorunu çözdüğünü de ekleyen Trump, skandalın basında bu kadar büyümesini "Seks, hisse senetlerinden daha iyi satar" sözleriyle yorumladı.
Krizin yankıları sürerken Trump’ın sosyal medyada paylaştığı yapay zekâ üretimi bir görsel tartışmaları daha da alevlendirdi. 2024 yılında uğradığı suikast girişimi sonrası çekilen ikonik fotoğrafına Jensen Huang ’ın yüzünü yerleştiren Trump, görselde yüzü kanlar içindeki Huang’ı elinde kırmızı bir sütyen tutarken ve arkasında Nvidia bayrağı dalgalanırken tasvir etti.
Ciddi bir casusluk soruşturmasını alaya alan bu paylaşım büyük tepki toplarken, Kongre üyeleri de harekete geçti. Trump’ın yakın müttefiklerinden eski Temsilciler Meclisi Başkanı Newt Gingrich bile Çinli bir casusla ilişki yaşayan bir ismin dünyanın en kritik çip şirketinin başına dönmesini "derinden yanlış" olarak nitelendirdi.
Senato Bankacılık Komitesi üyesi Demokrat Senatör Jack Reed ise 3 Aralık’ta komitede ifade verecek olan Huang ile Trump yönetimi ve Nvidia yönetim kurulu arasındaki tüm yazışmaların incelenmesi için soruşturma çağrısında bulundu.

Unsurprisingly, we’re already seeing some solid Black Friday deals on a wide variety of e-readers. Everything from the Kobo Libra Colour to last-gen Kindle Paperwhite is on sale, but if you’re looking for something much cheaper — or considerably smaller — the Xteink X4 Classic is in a league of its own. Thankfully, the tiny e-reader is down to a new low of $54.87 ($55 off) at Amazon , making it an especially affordable alternative to Amazon’s latest Kindle.
The X4 Classic is an updated version of Xteink’s original pocket-sized e-reader, one that features a miniature 4.3-inch E Ink display that makes it more pocketable than any current Kindle or Kobo model. Like the pricier X4 Pro — which also happens to be on sale direct from Xteink for $84 — it features both physical page-turning buttons and magnets that let you attach it to compatible smartphones. At just 2.4 ounces and 4.9mm thick, it’s also easy to slip into a pocket, while its larger 920mAh battery can last up to 10 days on a single charge.
That said, unlike the X4 Pro , the Classic lacks a touchscreen and built-in reading light, meaning you’ll need an external light to read in the dark. It also uses a proprietary magnetic charging connector instead of USB-C, and transferring books isn’t as straightforward as on a Kindle or Kobo. However, like the Pro, it does support the excellent CrossPoint Reader software , which you can install yourself to improve the reading experience. You can even use it to read books borrowed through Libby or purchased from stores like Kobo, though it takes a few extra steps to do so. Still, if you want an inexpensive, distraction-free way to read on the go, the X4 Classic is hard to beat for less than half the price of a Kindle.

The C825 can keep an eye on your home or help you keep in touch with your family.
TP-Link’s Tapo smart home brand announced a new indoor security camera that can help keep an eye on your house while you’re away or connect you to family and friends while you’re at home. The C825 upgrades a 2K pan-and-tilt camera with a 4-inch touchscreen, so when it’s not watching for intruders or misbehaving pets, it can be used to make hands-free video calls.
The Tapo C825 is available starting today for $149.99. That’s a little expensive for a 2K camera, but its tracking capabilities could make up for it not being 4K. Using a rotating base the C825 can pan 360 degrees while its camera module on top can tilt up and down up to 156 degrees. When paired with the camera’s 114.5-degree field of view every corner of a room should be covered, including in the middle of the night using its infrared night vision capabilities.
When used as a security camera the C825 leverages AI to differentiate between subjects including pets and different people through facial recognition. It can also recognize sounds and send alerts when a crying baby or barking dog is heard. The detection processing happens on-device, and videos of events are stored locally on a microSD card up to 512GB in size. No subscription is required, but you can upgrade to Tapo Care for a monthly fee , which adds cloud storage and features like video summaries and weekly reports.
While the C825’s two-way audio communication isn’t unique, expanding that to include two-way video is. Calls can be made to the C825 using the Tapo mobile app, but two of them can call each other directly by tapping a preconfigured onscreen contact. The device feels like another way for aging parents and grandparents to keep in touch with family without having to familiarize themselves with apps, phones, or tablets, but it’s also a useful hands-free video calling solution that can track and keep people in frame as they move around a room.
The C825’s touchscreen can be used as a digital photo frame, weather display, or a clock when you’re not in a video call. And for those times you don’t want the camera watching, you can configure privacy zones through the Tapo app or turn on a privacy mode that points the camera at the ceiling while pausing all monitoring.

Kalyan Krishnamurthy (pictured above), who steered Flipkart through Walmart’s acquisition in 2018 and helped build it into one of India’s biggest e-commerce companies, is stepping down as chief executive next week after more than 11 years with the company.
On Wednesday, Flipkart said it would announce Krishnamurthy’s successor in the coming weeks, and chief product and technology officer, Balaji Thiagarajan, will lead the company until a replacement is found.
A Walmart spokesperson told TechCrunch that Krishnamurthy’s last day at Flipkart will be December 4.
Krishnamurthy joined Flipkart in 2015 from Tiger Global, one of the company’s early investors, and became its CEO in 2017. He remained at the helm after Walmart acquired a controlling stake in the company for $16 billion in 2018.
Under Krishnamurthy, Flipkart said its business grew more than five-fold. The company has more than 500 million registered users and over 1.4 million sellers, including those on Shopsy, its low-cost shopping platform. The company’s marketplace offers over 150 million products across more than 80 categories.
Flipkart has of late moved into newer segments, including quick-commerce through Flipkart Minutes and, more recently, food delivery through a venture called Eat-in by Minutes . The expansion is targeted at Indian consumers who are increasingly turning to quick-delivery services for everything from groceries to electronics.
Thiagarajan joined Flipkart in September last year to lead its product and technology teams. Before that, he had founded Kasu.ai , a Bay Area startup working on AI assistants for corporate finance. He also previously worked at Google, Microsoft, and Uber in senior engineering positions, per his LinkedIn profile .
Krishnamurthy’s exit comes amid uncertainty around Flipkart’s IPO. In March, the company moved its headquarters from Singapore to India as part of its preparations to go public, but in May, Walmart reportedly told Flipkart to delay its IPO and focus on becoming profitable first .
Walmart declined to comment beyond its announcement when asked what prompted Krishnamurthy’s departure, and whether the leadership change would affect Flipkart’s IPO plans. Flipkart did not respond to a request for comment.
Founded in 2007 by Sachin and Binny Bansal as an online bookstore, much like its bigger rival Amazon, Flipkart eventually expanded into other categories. Under Krishnamurthy, it has grown into India’s largest online retailer by gross merchandise value, ahead of Amazon.
“Both Flipkart and Walmart are better because of Kalyan. We are grateful for his leadership, the governance he instilled and his many contributions to the company,” Chris Nicholas, president and CEO, Walmart International, said in a statement.

ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Amerikan hisse senedi piyasalarında giderek derinleşen satış dalgasını durdurmanın tek yolunun Jensen Huang'ı yeniden Nvidia'nın başına getirmek olduğuna karar verdi.
Konuya aşina çok sayıda kaynağın CNN'e verdiği bilgiye göre, Trump'ın geçen haftanın sonlarında aldığı bu karar, skandallarla gündeme gelen Huang'ın baskılar sonucu istifa etmesinden yalnızca 11 gün sonra görevine dönmesini sağlamak için Beyaz Saray'da benzeri görülmemiş bir girişimi tetikledi.
Hafta sonu gerçekleştirilen yoğun telefon görüşmelerinde, ABD Başkan Yardımcısı JD Vance öncülüğündeki üst düzey yetkililerin, Nvidia'nın yönetim kuruluna Huang'ı yeniden göreve getirmesi için baskı yaptığı iddia ediliyor.
Buna göre, yetkililer, Huang'ın Çin istihbaratıyla bağlantılı olduğundan şüphelenilen bir kadınla ilişkisine dair soru işaretleri devam etmesine rağmen şirket yönetimine, Huang'ın ulusal güvenlik açısından tehdit oluşturmadığı güvencesini verdi.
Trump da Nvidia'nın karar alma sürecine doğrudan müdahale ederek şirketin yönetim kurulunu bizzat aradı ve yakın müttefiki Huang'a kefil oldu.
Nvidia'nın pazartesi günü "hükümetin üst düzey yetkililerinden gelen görüşler" doğrultusunda Huang'ı yeniden CEO olarak atadığını duyurmasının ardından CNBC'ye konuşan Trump, şunları söyledi:
"Yönetim kuruluyla doğrudan ve dolaylı olarak görüşüyordum. Bu konuda çok güçlü bir kanaatim vardı. Bence büyük yıldızlarımızdan birini yeniden oyuna dahil ettik."
Beyaz Saray'ın yürüttüğü girişimin gizli tutulduğu, hatta Nvidia'nın bazı üst düzey çalışanları bile pazartesi sabahı yapılan açıklamadan kısa süre öncesine kadar gelişmelerden haberdar olmadığı aktarıldı.
CNN'e göre Trump ve diğer üst düzey yetkililer, Amerikan ekonomisinin giderek Nvidia ve bir avuç büyük yapay zeka şirketinin başarısına bağımlı hale geldiğini düşünüyor.
Huang'ın görevinden ayrılmasının ardından Nvidia hisseleri sert düşüş kaydetmiş, bu durum genel piyasalara da yansıyarak ABD'deki yapay zeka patlamasının sona ermek üzere olduğu yönündeki endişeleri körüklemişti.
Trump başlangıçta yatırımcıların güvenini yeniden kazanmak için Apple'ın eski CEO'su Tim Cook'un Nvidia'nın başına geçmesi ihtimalini gündeme getirdi. Ancak şirket, mali işlerden sorumlu üst düzey yöneticisi Colette Kress'i CEO olarak atadı.
Trump, pazartesi günü yaptığı açıklamada Kress'in geçen hafta CNBC'ye verdiği röportajdan etkilenmediğini söyledi.
ABD Başkanı, dört günlük Asya gezisinden cuma günü döndüğünde Amerikan borsaları tarihi nitelikteki beş günlük bir düşüş serisinin ortasındaydı. Trump ayrıca Çin Devlet Başkanı Şi Cinping'in de görüşmeleri sırasında Huang'dan övgüyle bahsettiğini aktardı.
Trump'ın eski danışmanı ve yakın müttefiki Steve Bannon, ABD Başkanı'nın 1929'daki borsa çöküşü ve ardından gelen Büyük Buhran'ın tekrarlanması ihtimalinden endişe duyduğunu ifade etti.
Daha önce Huang'ı "efsane" olarak nitelendiren Trump, danışmanlarına ve yetkililere piyasaların istikrara kavuşması için Nvidia'nın eski CEO'sunun görevine dönmesi gerektiğini söyledi.
İddiaya göre, Trump, Silikon Vadisi'nin nüfuzlu isimleriyle yakın ilişkileri olan Başkan Yardımcısı Vance'i bu girişimi yönetmekle görevlendirdi.
CNN'e konuşan kaynaklara göre Vance, takip eden 72 saat boyunca Huang'la doğrudan koordinasyon içinde çalışarak Nvidia'nın yönetim kuruluna baskı yaptı.
Bu süreçte şirket yönetimine, hükümetin Huang'ın ulusal güvenliği tehlikeye atabilecek yasa dışı veya uygunsuz bir eylemde bulunduğuna dair herhangi bir kanıt tespit etmediği güvencesi verildi.
ABD Adalet Bakanı Todd Blanche'ın da hafta sonu Trump'a, devam eden soruşturmalar kapsamında Jensen Huang veya Nvidia'nın herhangi bir yasa dışı eylemine ilişkin kanıt bulunmadığını bildirdiği aktarıldı.
Söz konusu soruşturmalar, ABD'nin ihracat kontrollerini ihlal ettiğinden şüphelenilen Alice Huang ve onunla bağlantılı şirketlere odaklanıyor.
Ancak Blanche, Huang'ın yeniden göreve getirilmesinin ardından Fox News'te kendisine yöneltilen, Nvidia CEO'sunun ulusal güvenlik endişelerinden veya olası yasa ihlallerinden tamamen aklanıp aklanmadığı sorusunu yanıtsız bıraktı.
Ticaret Bakanı Howard Lutnick ve Hazine Bakanı Scott Bessent'in de Huang'ın göreve dönmesini sağlayan girişimde rol aldığı belirtildi.
Vance ve diğer üst düzey yetkililer, istihbarat kurumlarının uyarılarının önemini azaltmaya çalışırken Huang'ın eşsiz bir yetenek olduğunu ve ABD'nin yapay zeka alanında Çin karşısındaki üstünlüğünü koruması açısından kritik önem taşıdığını savundu.
Nvidia'nın yönetim kurulu, yalnızca dört gün önce yatırımcılarla yaptığı bir görüşmede Huang'ın yeniden göreve getirilmesi çağrılarını reddetmiş, davranışlarının şirketin etik kuralları, standartları ve kurum kültürüyle bağdaşmadığını açıklamıştı.
Ancak Trump yönetiminin yoğun baskısının ardından yönetim kurulu pazar akşamı kararını değiştirdiğini ve Huang'ın dönüşünü ertesi sabah duyuracağını yetkililere bildirdi.
Huang'ın evlilik dışı ilişki yaşadığını kabul etmesinin ardından ABD Kongresi'nde hem Demokratların hem de Cumhuriyetçilerin desteğiyle, CEO'nun davranışları ve bunların ulusal güvenlik açısından olası sonuçlarına ilişkin soruşturmalar başlatılmıştı.
Skandal, Trump ve üst düzey danışmanlarının Çin hükümeti adına çalıştığından şüphelenilen Alice Huang hakkında daha önce yapılan uyarıları nasıl ele aldığını da tartışmaya açtı.
Alice Huang, Nvidia'dan çip satın alan Megaspeed adlı şirkette yöneticilik yapıyordu. ABD'li yetkililer, bu çiplerin daha sonra Çin'e ulaştırılmış olabileceğinden endişe ediyor.
Jensen Huang ise sektörün gelişmiş yapay zeka çiplerinin bir bölümünün Çin'e satışına izin verilmesi için Beyaz Saray nezdinde yürüttüğü lobi faaliyetlerine öncülük etmişti.
Şimdi Kongre'de, Huang'ın Alice Huang'la ilişkisinin çiplerin yasa dışı yollarla Çin'e ulaştırılmasını kolaylaştırıp kolaylaştırmadığı araştırılıyor.
Alice Huang'ın Çin istihbaratıyla bağlantılarının tam niteliği henüz netlik kazanmış değil. Ancak Çin'in ulusal güvenlik mevzuatı, vatandaşlarının talep edilmesi halinde istihbarat faaliyetlerine yardımcı olmasını zorunlu kılıyor.
Bazı ABD'li yetkililer, bu durumun tek başına bile söz konusu ilişkiyi karşı istihbarat açısından riskli hale getirdiğini düşünüyor. Alice Huang'ın Jensen Huang aracılığıyla ABD Başkanı'na dolaylı erişim sağlayabilme ihtimali de bu endişeleri artırıyor.
Çin'e karşı daha sert bir politika izlenmesini uzun süredir savunan ABD Dışişleri Bakanı Marco Rubio'nun, yılın başlarında Trump ve diğer yetkilileri Huang'ın ilişkisi konusunda defalarca uyardığı belirtiliyor.
Rubio, skandalın patlak vermesinden bu yana kamuoyuna açıklama yapmaktan kaçınırken pazartesi günü de Huang'ın yeniden atanmasına ilişkin gazetecilerin sorularını yanıtsız bıraktı.
Öte yandan ABD Ticaret Bakanlığı, Megaspeed'i Amerikan ürünlerine erişimini kısıtlayacak olan ihracat kontrol listesine (Entity List) dahil ediyor.
Huang'ın yeniden göreve getirilmesi Beyaz Saray'ın bazı kesimlerinde ve Silikon Vadisi'nde sevinçle karşılandı.
Karar, Trump'a doğrudan erişim imkanına sahip bir avuç teknoloji milyarderinin Amerikan siyasetindeki nüfuzunun son örneklerinden biri olarak değerlendirildi.
Trump'ın Huang konusunda görüşüne başvurduğunu açıkladığı Elon Musk, X hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda, "Hata düzeltildi," ifadelerini kullandı.
Ancak Trump'ın yakın çevresindeki bazı isimler, ABD Başkanı'nın özel bir şirketin yönetim kararlarına doğrudan müdahale etmesinden rahatsızlık duydu.
Nebraska'nın Cumhuriyetçi Senatörü Pete Ricketts de X hesabından yaptığı açıklamada karara tepki gösterdi.
"Jensen Huang, aralarında astlarının ve Çin casusu olduğu iddia edilen bir kişinin de bulunduğu kişilerle birden fazla ilişki yaşadı. Davranışları yeniden göreve getirilmesini haklı çıkarmıyor."
Trump'ın bazı danışmanları, Nvidia'nın Beyaz Saray'ın talebi doğrultusunda Huang'ı yeniden göreve getirmesinin, ocak ayında Demokratların kontrolüne geçecek Kongre'de yeni bir soruşturma dalgasına zemin hazırlayabileceğini düşünüyor.
Bazı danışmanların, Huang'ın davranışlar…

Companies like Akai have decided to embrace the modding community rather than resist vibe coders.
The emergence of powerful vibe-coding agents and tools like Reverse Engineer Anything has caused chaos in the music gear world , leaving companies scrambling to figure out how to respond. While some, like Roland, have remained silent for now, others have embraced the modding community. In the last several weeks, as it’s become clear that no piece of music gear is safe from Claude and a subreddit full of curious tinkerers, companies have begun making more and more of their devices open source.
The biggest name to decide “if you can’t beat ’em, join ’em” is inMusic , the parent company of Akai, Moog, Native Instruments, and more. “We’re going to provide a toolbox to the community, we’re going to provide the inner workings of, say, an MPC or Sample so that people can do what they want,” inMusic CEO Jack O’Donnell tells The Verge . That includes a recently launched SDK and several open-source devices, including the recently teased MPC Sample Key .
Akai is trying to walk a fine line, offering modders access while keeping its products reliable for professionals. O’Donnell says the company will “try to give them a reset button” so “they can experiment with it, and then not lose what they have.”
Behringer has also rushed to cash in, announcing a slew of open-source devices. In just a matter of weeks, it announced a $150 clone of the MPC One called Kick , a clone of the E-mu SP-1200 , the Anima DJ controller , the Ignite sequencer, and the Polykeys 61 MIDI controller, all of which are open source. It’s unclear when any of these products might launch.
M-Vave’s FM-1 helped kick-start the whole movement. The $70 pocketable clone of the iconic Yamaha DX7 became the synth of the summer not just because of its dirt-cheap price and faithfully re-created ’80s tones, but because it also turned out to be infinitely hackable. There are well over a dozen different custom firmwares for the FM-1. M-Vave responded by releasing an open-source firmware with more features for developers to build on. The company also confirmed that a successor, the FM-2, is in development and will be open source as well.
Other companies have also embraced the modding community. Erica Synths recently released the source code for its LXR-02 drum machine , but founder Ģirts Ozoliņš isn’t necessarily fully on board with vibe coding. “Inventions succeed if they solve some fundamental problems, right?” he tells The Verge . “So, I’m still wondering what fundamental problem vibe coding solves.”
While he can’t imagine a producer simply stacking his studio with a bunch of hacked FM-1s running various synth engines, he’s curious to see what the community cooks up for the LXR. And he does see a benefit in making music tech a little less disposable. “What I like on the upside of this is that there is some trace of sustainability. Instead of buying five or 10 plastic boxes, you can try options on one,” he says, though he’s under no illusions about the environmental impact of vibe coding. “Of course it by far does not offset data center impact on the planet and on ecology and stuff like that.”
Polyend has also gotten on board, open-sourcing its line of Tracker grooveboxes. The Polish company’s decision to open its arms to vibe coders isn’t too much of a surprise. Last year it released the Endless guitar pedal, which lets users vibe-code their own effects. Opening its other instruments to AI tinkering feels like a natural extension.
Elektron is less thrilled about the emergence of vibe-coded mods. The company banned links to custom firmware from its official forums, saying, “We would always warn against modifications to our firmware and/or machines that could brick them (potentially rendering them unusable), prevent future updates, affect warranty coverage.”
Elektron’s CPO Christian Alsing told YouTuber EZBOT that he was sympathetic to the hacker community and that the company has roots there with its first instrument, the Sidstation (based on the iconic SID sound chip from the Commodore 64). He also said that he believes users have a right to modify their devices as they see fit. But he pushed back on the idea that Elektron is “withholding features,” an accusation that Akai also faced .
Ģirts also defended Elektron, saying, “people tend to blame the company, saying they are hiding features ... you design an instrument, you have a specific concept in mind, and you cannot foresee millions of possibilities ... it’s not about hiding features; it’s more about having an idea of how an instrument should look and work.”
Other major music manufacturers, like Roland, Korg, Arturia, and Novation – all of whom did not comment for this story – have yet to issue any public statements about the explosion of AI-aided custom firmwares.

Honours students are increasingly being asked to sit oral assessments – but at the University of Sydney it’s become a requirement for all

When Aidan Elwig Pollock signed up for an honours program at the University of Sydney, he did not expect his 20,000-word thesis to be accompanied by a spoken component.
But, as AI increasingly makes written research an unreliable form of assessment, the university has demanded all students taking the one-year program defend their arguments in conversation with professors.
Top Australian universities are increasingly asking honours students to sit oral assessments, with Sydney the first known to require it across honours programs.
Exams have moved from computers back to paper or interviews in the four years since the release of ChatGPT made AI plagiarism a concern. Some educators have adopted the debate-focused tutorials traditional at Oxbridge colleges or the viva voce assessments typical of PhDs.
But honours programs – a year of intensive research for dedicated students after their bachelor’s degree – have been slower to adapt as they’re typically focused on a single project, which accounts for most of their grade.
Elwig Pollock, a history student, said he had not used AI at all on his work on how the commemoration of Captain Cook has evolved over time, and that the new demand was “insulting” to students and the professors who supervise them.
“If you’ve used AI to do your honours thesis and your supervisor has not figured it out throughout your regular meetings, then what’s stopping you from communicating that material successfully in a 15-minute conversation,” Elwig Pollock said.
Since 2024, Sydney bachelor’s degrees have included a mix of assessments that are vulnerable or secure to AI tools. This year, the university has formally extended that to honours programs, though the format is different for every faculty.
On Wednesday, Elwig Pollock had a short conversation which was a pass or fail hurdle task but was worth nothing towards his final grade. In his case most of his marks are coming from his thesis but his degree will not be awarded if he fails the conversation.
Engineering student Isabelle* had an entirely different experience.
Last week, the University of Sydney student had an hour of interviews with professors in a single room with five classmates, as the school rushed through assessing 250 students in two days. It accounted for 50% of her grade.
“There were people coming in and out of the room while we were being assessed so it was distracting,” said Isabelle, who asked for a pseudonym to avoid being penalised.
“[We had to] move to the other side of the room so my marker could hear me.”
The change has stressed students who aren’t used to speaking up in class, don’t speak English as a first language or need their honours to become qualified in their field – including engineers like Isabelle.
“I think it’s particularly bad in engineering because writing skills are poor, but I think it’s a Band-Aid solution,” she said of the verbal component.
Adam Bridgeman, the university’s acting deputy vice-chancellor for education, said honours degrees needed to change.
“We necessarily treat honours theses as open assessments as we can’t reliably restrict AI use,” Bridgeman said.
Staff and students were offered guidance and practice to manage the transformation and ensure English fluency and speaking ability were not “inadvertently rewarded”, he said.
“We appreciate some students might be nervous about the experience, especially if it’s their first time,” Bridgeman said. “We’ll take feedback on board as we plan for 2027 assessments.”
While Sydney is the only major institution to mandate interviews for honours programs, schools at the University of Melbourne, Monash University and Australian Catholic University are bringing them in.
Adelaide University, which was previously among the first in Australia to reintroduce viva voce tasks, is using “interactive oral assessments” in which students and teachers role-play real-world professional situations.
There are no public reports of Australian honours students cheating with AI. Kurt Iveson, an honours coordinator for Sydney’s School of Geosciences, said the change was still needed to respond to AI’s growing role in education.
“They’re not the kind of people that I would personally be worried about getting Claude to write their honours thesis for them,” Iveson said.
“But … [management] want to be able to demonstrate to the world, as part of their social licence and external accreditation, that things are being assessed securely.”
The interviews are a heavy addition to professors’ workloads – and no casuals have been brought on to help. Staff and students contacted by Guardian Australia said the new rules had left supervisors feeling rushed and overworked.
But, Iveson said, interviews are a valuable way of helping students learn and understand the significance of their research.
“Assuming that you have actually written it, you know your shit, you’ll be fine, and you’ll have a good conversation.”

Altın fiyatlarında satış baskısı sürüyor. Ons altın çarşamba sabahı 3 bin 546 dolara gerilerken, geçen cuma görülen 14 ayın en düşük seviyesi yeniden piyasaların gündemine oturdu. Peki altın neden düşüyor? Altının düşmesine neden olan 3 etken uzmanlar tarafından açıklandı.
Ons altın, 25 Kasım Çarşamba sabahı saat 07.40 itibarıyla bir önceki kapanışa göre yüzde 0,15 değer kaybederek 3 bin 546 dolardan alıcı buldu. Bu seviye, geçen cuma görülen 3 bin 502 dolarlık dip noktaya yalnızca 44 dolar uzaklıkta. Piyasada şimdi konuşulan soru, o dibin yeniden test edilip edilmeyeceği.
İç piyasada da tablo farklı değil. Gram altın aynı saatlerde 5 bin 776 TL seviyelerinde işlem görüyor. Yatırımcıların gözü ise haftanın en kritik verisi olarak görülen ABD PCE fiyat endeksinde. Fed'in enflasyonu izlerken baktığı bu gösterge, faiz patikasına dair beklentileri doğrudan değiştirebilecek güçte.
Altındaki geri çekilmenin başını Fed çekiyor. Son günlerde Fed yetkililerinden gelen şahin mesajlar, ek faiz artırımı beklentisini güçlendirdi. Piyasa fiyatlamalarına göre aralık toplantısında 25 baz puanlık artış ihtimali yüzde 96 civarında; ocak ayında yeni bir artış da masada.
Faiz getirisi sunmayan altın için bu tablo kötü haber anlamına geliyor. Faizler yükseldikçe mevduat ve tahvil gibi getirili araçlar cazip hale geliyor, sarı metali elde tutmanın maliyeti ise artıyor. Altının son haftalardaki zayıf seyrinde bu beklentinin payı büyük.
İkinci neden borsalardan geliyor. Yapay zeka yatırımlarına yönelik endişeler teknoloji hisselerinde satış dalgasını tetikledi ve piyasalarda likidite baskısı arttı. Nvidia CEO'su Jensen Huang'ın etkisiyle başlayan toparlanma kısa sürede sönünce altın da yeniden aşağı yönlü hareket etti. Borsada kaybeden yatırımcıların nakde dönmek için altın pozisyonlarını bozması, düşüşü derinleştiren etkenlerden biri olarak görülüyor.
Üçüncü neden ise Washington'da. Trump yönetimi, ABD Yüksek Mahkemesi'nin iptal ettiği gümrük vergilerinin yerine yeni bir tarife planı hazırlıyor. Yeni vergi tehditleri Asya borsalarında, özellikle çip ağırlıklı piyasalarda sert düşüşlere yol açtı.
Diğer değerli metaller de kayıpta. Gümüşün onsu sabah saatlerinde yüzde 0, 29 düşüşle 40,70 dolardan işlem gördü. Platin yüzde 1,39 gerileyerek bin 258 dolara, paladyum ise yüzde 0,14 düşüşle 852 dolara indi.

Şile Belediyesine yönelik yolsuzluk soruşturması kapsamında açılan davanın 11'inci duruşmasında, tutuklu bulunduğu Çorlu Cezaevi'nden getirilen şarkıcı Haluk Levent tanık olarak dinlendi. Asistanı Yeliz Kaya'nın banka hesaplarını kendisinin kullandığını söyleyen Levent, Kaya'nın Şile dosyasıyla bağlantısı olmadığını savundu.
Geçmişten kalan icra ve haciz dosyaları nedeniyle bazı arkadaşlarına ait banka hesaplarını kullandığını anlatan Haluk Levent, bu durumu daha önce ilgili kurumlara da bildirdiğini belirtti. Asistanı Yeliz Kaya'nın tutukluluğuna ilişkin konuşan Levent, "Onun yerine benim tutuklanmam gerekiyor" dedi.
Davada tutuklu yargılanan kardeşi Berkant Acil ile arasındaki para transferlerine de değinen Levent, bunların şahsi borç ilişkisine dayandığını savundu. Kardeşiyle yaptığı yazışmalarda rüşvet veya ihaleye ilişkin herhangi bir ifade bulunmadığını ileri sürdü.
Cezaevindeki koşullarına ilişkin de konuşan Haluk Levent, 4,5 aydır tek başına bir hücrede kaldığını belirtti. Ahbap Derneği hakkındaki iddialara yanıt veren sanatçı, kişisel borç ilişkilerinin derneğin mali işlemleriyle karıştırıldığını savundu.
Duruşmada söz alan Berkant Acil, altı aydır görmediğini söylediği ağabeyine özlemini dile getirdi. Yarın doğum günü olan Haluk Levent'in doğum gününü de mahkeme salonunda kutladı.
Haberler.com'da yer alan yorumlar, kullanıcıların kişisel görüşlerini yansıtır ve haberler.com'un editöryal politikası ile örtüşmeyebilir. Yorumların hukuki sorumluluğu tamamen yazarlarına aittir.

İngiltere Prensi Harry'nin eşi Sussex Düşesi Meghan Markle'ın babası Thomas Markle hakkında ABD'de çocuklara yönelik cinsel istismar görüntüleri bulundurduğu iddiasıyla iki ayrı federal suçlama yöneltildi. 82 yaşındaki Markle'ın her bir suçlamadan 20 yıla kadar hapis cezası alabileceği belirtildi.
ABD'nin Florida eyaletinde 6 Kasım'da FBI tarafından gözaltına alınan Thomas Markle hakkında Los Angeles'taki federal büyük jüri tarafından iddianame hazırlandı. Markle, iki farklı tarihte çocuklara yönelik cinsel istismar görüntüleri içeren materyalleri bilerek bulundurmakla suçlandı.
Soruşturma kapsamında Markle'ın Los Angeles'ta yaklaşık 20 yıldır kiraladığı depoda arama yapıldı. Federal ajanların aramalarda suçlamalara konu olan görüntüleri ele geçirdiği belirtildi. Savcılık, bazı görüntülerde Markle'ın da bulunduğunun bir tanık tarafından ileri sürüldüğünü aktardı.
Geçirdiği felcin ardından 2025 yılında Filipinler'e taşınan Thomas Markle hakkında soruşturmanın, oğlu Thomas Markle Jr.'ın ihbarıyla başladığı ortaya çıktı. Babasının eşyaları arasında çocuklara yönelik cinsel istismar görüntüleri bulduğunu öne süren Markle Jr., Filipinler polisine ve FBI'a başvurmuştu.
ABD Savcısı Bill Essayli, Markle'ın suçlu bulunması halinde her bir suçlama için 20 yıla kadar hapis cezası alabileceğini açıkladı. Filipinler'de de hakkında üç ayrı suç duyurusunda bulunulan Markle'ın önümüzdeki haftalarda Los Angeles'ta hakim karşısına çıkması bekleniyor.
Geçtiğimiz hafta Florida'da bir hakim, Markle'ın yargılanabilecek zihinsel yeterliliğe sahip olduğuna karar vermişti.

France blames an Iranian cyber unit for sabotaging hundreds of supermarket freezers.
One night in October, hackers staged one of the most unusual cyber attacks in history : cranking up the temperature in refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets across France and destroying millions of euros of food.
Hackers have targeted commercial fridges and freezers before, but never at this scale and never in the heart of Europe. The brazen attack left cyber professionals unsure as to who might have executed such a madcap operation. But French intelligence agencies found traces of Farsi and other clues in the digital trail pointing to an elite hacking unit of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
The unit allegedly behind the hack, Shahid Kaveh, was already well known to Western intelligence agencies. Named after Mahmoud Kaveh, an Iranian commander who died during the 1980s Iran-Iraq war, it is one of several hacking units overseen by the Revolutionary Guards’ Cyber Electronic Command.
The group, which often goes by the online persona CyberAv3ngers, has a history of targeting critical infrastructure. In 2023 and 2024, it hacked Israeli-made industrial control devices inside water, manufacturing, and transportation systems across several US states. Operational disruption was minimal, but the attackers left a message each time: “Every equipment ‘made in Israel’ is CyberAv3ngers legal target.”
State-backed Iranian hackers have rarely targeted Europe in this way, however. October’s hacks, experts say, mark an escalation in the Islamic republic’s cyber warfare strategy and a new willingness to hit European infrastructure.
“Iran has very clearly messaged that the global economy will be disrupted as a consequence of it being shut out from the world,” said Ellie Geranmayeh of the European Council on Foreign Relations.
While France and other European countries have largely stayed out of the US and Israel’s campaign against Iran, which started in February, the Islamic republic increasingly views all Nato countries as legitimate targets, she continued. “This is about sowing panic in Europe and increasing that global pain threshold.”
Similar attacks were staged this month against supermarkets in 10 other countries across Europe, though no group has yet been blamed.
Iran has denied any role in the freezer hacks, but France is seeking international arrest warrants for three Iranians allegedly involved: Hamid Reza Lashgarian, believed by US intelligence to be head of the Guards’ Cyber Electronic Command, and two Shahid Kaveh leaders, 37-year-old Mahdi Lashgarian and 35-year-old Reza Salarvand. Both Lashgarians were placed under US sanctions in 2024.
Often staffed with young engineers and software developers, the Revolutionary Guards’ cyber units have developed formidable skills in espionage and cyber warfare.
“Iran is a country of engineers, and people continue to underestimate its capabilities,” said Sanam Vakil, Middle East director at Chatham House think-tank. “It has a long history of successful cyber operations,” she added, noting that Iran had learnt through its own experience of cyber attacks, most notably the Stuxnet assault on its nuclear program by the US and Israel in 2009.
French intelligence agencies have said the group used a Chinese-made scanning tool to scour the public Internet for connected refrigeration units. Infrastructure linked to the group also conducted reconnaissance using Modbus, a digital language widely used to control industrial machinery—a technique Shahid Kaveh has employed since at least April, according to the authorities.
The modus operandi described by the French authorities was consistent with the Iranian attacks in the US in 2023 and 2024, said Cynthia Kaiser, former deputy cyber director at the FBI. Near-identical hacks to those have taken place this year, though CyberAv3ngers did not claim responsibility, and US authorities stopped short of explicitly blaming Iran.
Kaiser said it was also possible that a third state could have contracted Shahid Kaveh to conduct the European attacks. “Even if Iranians were behind the keyboard, these attacks really appear more consistent with Russian-type targeting,” she said. “It wouldn’t surprise me if we eventually uncovered collaboration behind the scenes.”
Russia, like Iran, has sophisticated cyber capabilities and has shown increasing willingness to use them against Europe.
Vakil at Chatham House acknowledged Russian involvement remained a possibility, noting that the strength of the relationship between the two countries was often under-appreciated by Western officials. “Their ties have grown through the context of these wars,” she said, referring to Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine and Iran’s conflict with the US and Israel. In March, Russian state-sponsored hacking group NoName claimed responsibility for a series of attacks on Israeli targets.
Whether or not Shahid Kaveh was working on behalf of Moscow or another power, the operation would have to be sanctioned by the senior leadership of the IRGC, according to Gil Messing, chief of staff at Israeli cyber security group Check Point Software.
Cyber weapons have a limited shelf life, as once a specific software or hardware vulnerability has been exploited, it tends to be almost immediately patched by other potential targets.
“The decision to make such a thing and burn out this capability is something that would have to be authorized by senior levels,” Messing said. “This is not a very sophisticated attack, but it sends a very strong message.”
