FILE - Senegal's Sadio Mane holds the trophy aloft as he celebrates with teammates after winning the Africa Cup of Nations final soccer match between Senegal and Morocco in Rabat, Morocco, Sunday, Jan. 18, 2026. Youssef Loulidi/AP hide caption
More than 10 months on from a chaotic, controversial final, Senegal is Africa's soccer champion once again.
Senegal won back the Africa Cup of Nations title in a legal fight on Tuesday after the Court of Arbitration for Sport overturned an earlier ruling which handed the trophy to Morocco.
Senegal won the Africa Cup on the field in Morocco in January and then lost it in a legal case in March because its players walked off the field in protest in second-half stoppage time.
CAS has now rejected that earlier ruling, based on referee Jean-Jacques Ndala's decision to let the game resume after the protest.
"The Court of Arbitration for Sport has delivered justice to sport," Senegalese soccer federation president Abdoulaye Fall said in a statement.
The legal battle may not be over yet after Morocco announced plans to appeal, likely to Switzerland's supreme court, in a challenge to the integrity of a senior CAS judge.
Tournament regulations said a team which refuses to play should be considered to have lost the game, but CAS said those rules were meant only for cases "when a team's conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently."
Ndala "did not err in law" when he resumed the game and had "sole authority" to make that call, CAS said, adding its three judges were unanimous.
"The panel acknowledged that the referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension," CAS said. "However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as 'arbitrary.' On the contrary, the referee's judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game."
Morocco's soccer federation detailed plans for an appeal that targets one of the three judges on the CAS panel.
In a statement, the Moroccan federation protested what it described as the court's failure to address potential integrity concerns, alleging "confirmed communication" between German arbitrator Ulrich Haas and Fall, the Senegalese soccer president, 48 hours before the decision was issued.
The CAS director general, Matthieu Reeb, acknowledged to reporters at the court in Lausanne that a Moroccan protest was received just minutes before the verdict was announced.
Reeb said the court's panel "in charge of petitions for challenge has conceded that there was not enough elements at this stage to postpone the notification of the award."
CAS verdicts can be challenged at Switzerland's supreme court, also in Lausanne, though only on limited procedural grounds of which a judge's integrity could be one.
Haas has been among the most respected and in-demand CAS judges in the past 20 years, selected by parties in storied cases involving Manchester City's beating a Champions League ban by UEFA, tennis star Simona Halep's doping case and Africa's Champions League final in 2019.
Patrick Kabou, a lawyer for the Senegalese Soccer Federation, called the alleged communication between Fall and Haas "unreal."
Senegal won the final 1-0 after extra time with chaos on the field and violent clashes in the stands. Even the ball boys were involved in scuffles as they tried to snatch towels that Senegal goalkeeper Edouard Mendy was using to keep his gloves dry.
The result was overturned two months later as a 3-0 default win for Morocco by an appeals panel appointed by the Confederation of African Football (CAF).
Senegal beat AFCON host nation Morocco after a 15-minute delay in play. At 0-0, Senegal's team walked off the field to protest Morocco being awarded a penalty kick in the last minute of regulation time.
Match referee Ndala of Congo eventually allowed the game to restart, Morocco's penalty by Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz — a slow chip shot known as a "Panenka" — was saved, and Senegal won in extra time.
The drama continued through the months of legal tussles. Senegal's players paraded with the trophy ahead of a game in March against Peru, even though Morocco was recognized as the champion at that point.
Both teams played at the World Cup believing themselves to be the rightful champion of Africa.
Senegal had the laws of the game on its side, and Morocco had the tournament regulations.
The laws of soccer state that referee decisions are final. CAS backed that position with its own "field of play" doctrine, that on-field calls by a referee generally can't be taken to the sports court.
"By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met — both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume," CAS said.
In the first legal case in March, CAF appeal judges cited AFCON tournament regulations that if a team "refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorization of the referee, it shall be considered loser and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition."
The CAS judges heard evidence at a one-day hearing last month and the court promised a verdict by the end of November with a full written ruling of its judges setting out reasons for their decision.
The next men's AFCON starts in June co-hosted by Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania. Morocco will aim to end a wait for the title which now stands at 50 years.
"Senegal won on the pitch, and the court simply confirmed what we all already knew: We are the real champions of Africa," said Mariama Sidibé, 35, an accountant in the capital, Dakar.
Sidibé said the dispute between Morocco and Senegal should now be left in the past.
"With all of this behind us, we should focus on what unites us now, and who knows, maybe Morocco can have its revenge on the field during the next AFCON this summer," she said.
"At the end of the day Morocco and Senegal are brothers," Sidibé added, referring to the countries' long shared close ties built on religion, trade and culture.
Sidi Sylla, a philosophy student at Dakar's main university, said the court's ruling was "not just a win for Senegal but for football in general."
CAS rulings have stripped many athletes of Olympic medals for doping, but it's rare to overturn the result of a major soccer competition.
CAS refused to change the results of the 2019 Asian Cup, dismissing an appeal that the star striker on winning team Qatar shouldn't have been eligible for the tournament.
A lengthy legal battle over the same year's African Champions League final also ended with the original winner, Esperance of Tunisia, taking the title after its opponent Wydad from Morocco refused to play on.
One notable CAS ruling on a team sport title came at the Winter Olympics in 2022. A doping case involving then-15-year-old Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva ended up with her disqualification, and the Russian team being dropped from gold to bronze in the team event.

Americans are opting for smaller gatherings, reconsidering travel or swapping expensive ingredients for cheaper alternatives
Thanksgiving is just one day away, but for some Americans, the holiday may look a little different this year as higher costs for food, drinks , household goods, air travel and gasoline have prompted some families to rethink their plans and spending.
The Guardian recently asked readers across the United States how they were marking the holiday this year and whether higher prices had affected their plans or made them rethink their usual traditions.
While some said their plans remained unchanged, many said that they were scaling back and cutting costs. Some said that they were opting for smaller gatherings, reconsidering travel or choosing not to host at all. Others said they were swapping more expensive ingredients for cheaper alternatives or cooking less than they normally would.
In Florida, one man in his 60s said that he and his girlfriend were “scaling way back” this year.
“The expense has made it impossible for us to have what we usually do,” he said, adding that “food is horribly expensive”.
Instead of doing three different pies, they are preparing just one this year, along with a single side dish.
Cindy Van Vreede, 66, in Wisconsin, told the Guardian that the senior center where she goes for “free meals several times a week, is offering to bring a free Thanksgiving dinner to me at my home”.
“By not traveling or expected to bring a dish, I am saving money staying at home,” she said. “I’m also saving money on gas because I’m not driving my car two hours each way.”
A recent report from the American Farm Bureau Federation estimated that Americans preparing a Thanksgiving meal will face “higher prices overall this year”, with the average cost of a 10-person dinner up 6% from last year. It marks the first time since 2022 that American shoppers will see an increase “in the price of goods for Thanksgiving dinner”, according to the report.
The increase for this year is “largely driven by increased prices for Thanksgiving staples such as turkey, milk, rolls and cranberries”, the report says, noting the increases “aren’t a complete surprise as the effects of significant spikes in prices for critical inputs throughout the supply chain, like fuel for processing and transportation, have made their way to consumers”.
America’s farmers and ranchers, the report states, are also facing “significant challenges, with record diesel costs, elevated fertilizer prices, increased labor expenses, and a bigger bill for items like rent and electricity – all of which hurt their ability to breakeven at the end of the year”.
In Texas, 55-year-old Cheryl said that she was “probably not going to celebrate this year”.
“I’ll miss it, just getting together with my family,” she said, “but we can’t afford the food, and going to a friend’s house is unlikely, too.”
Cheryl said that she has watched as her “regular weekly groceries have gone up so much it’s getting harder to afford them”.
Others are finding ways to preserve some of their traditions while spending less.
In Virginia, 39-year-old Hannah told the Guardian: “We’re going low-key.”
“This year, I’m sticking with a few essential dishes – turkey, gravy, potatoes, cranberries, and mac and cheese,” she said. “I’m using recipes that use cheaper ingredients. I’m having my 10-year-old make Kraft mac and cheese from the box rather than using a homemade recipe with more expensive cheeses.”
Hannah said that she was spending “more time than ever looking at prices at different stores, and I’ve been using store loyalty programs to squeeze extra savings”.
A recent survey by Lending Tree found that, among those planning to celebrate Thanksgiving, more than half said that inflation was affecting their plans or budget, with 25% saying that they are changing their food choices as a result, 22% saying they are using more coupons and 14% saying they are cutting back on guests.
The survey also found that nearly two-thirds of respondents said that they may need to borrow to host Thanksgiving, including 38% who said they planned to use credit cards to cover the costs.
In Seattle, Liliya told the Guardian that she was trying to persuade her partner “not to order the whole turkey but to buy a few cuts instead”.
Their Thanksgiving, she said, “will be a very small family gathering, no different from other years outside of me trying to scale down on the turkey”.
For others, the expense of traveling for the holiday has prompted a change of plans. A woman in North Carolina said that she had decided not to travel this year, partly due to the cost of “fuel and lodging”.
Instead, she said, they will be treating themselves to a restaurant meal.

FILE - Chen Jining, Communist Party Secretary for Shanghai attends a deliberation on the government work report, on the sideline of the National People's Congress at the Beijing Hotel, March 6, 2025. Ng Han Guan/AP hide caption
BANGKOK — Chinese Communist Party authorities are investigating Shanghai party secretary Chen Jining for suspected violations of party discipline, China's anti-corruption watchdog said Tuesday.
The Politburo member is the latest senior official targeted in President Xi Jinping's long-running anti-corruption campaign, which has shown no signs of letting up in scope or depth.
Chen is under investigation by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection. The brief announcement by China's Central Commission for Discipline Inspection provided no further details.
A statement released by the Shanghai city government said the Standing Committee of the Shanghai Committee of the CCP "expressed firm support" for the decision to investigate Chen.
The decision sent "a clear and powerful signal that the fight against corruption would continue without pause or retreat," but with "a firm determination to win," the statement said.
The investigation follows sweeping purges under Xi, who has emphasized greater party discipline. The Chinese leader has pursued an anti-corruption campaign for more than a decade, carrying out purges on a scale not seen since Mao Zedong's rule.
"The takedown again shows that Xi Jinping's anti-corruption campaign has no limits," Mingda Qiu, a senior analyst at Eurasia Group, said in an emailed statement. "This is the fourth Politburo member to fall, and the fourth sitting member brought down in the current cycle. The pattern is unprecedented."
The recent Politburo purges highlight how much Chinese politics depend on shifting circumstances, with even officials with qualities that Xi apparently valued being vulnerable to removal, said Joseph Torigian, a professor at American University based in Washington.
"On paper," they appear to be "individuals Xi would appreciate," Torigian said, but afterward, "we could easily come up with hypotheses for why he got rid of them."
Other Politburo members purged include Gen. Zhang Youxia and He Weidong, both senior members of the Central Military Commission, which oversees the armed forces, and Ma Xingrui, a provincial party secretary.
The post of Shanghai party secretary has traditionally been viewed as a stepping stone to China's top leadership. The country's former President Jiang Zemin, its current premier, Li Qiang, and Xi himself previously held the position.
Chen has served as Shanghai party secretary since 2022. He previously held senior positions in Beijing's municipal government and headed the Ministry of Environmental Protection.

After African football was dragged into needless disrepute the next step is to tackle two key areas of governance
A journey of 310 days and three legal proceedings to confirm two things we know – that Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 to win the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and, most importantly, that the decision of a referee remains final and sacrosanct – has produced the longest, most comical and embarrassing Afcon final in the tournament’s 69-year history.
As the Confederation of African Football (Caf) executive committee member Samir Sobha told the Guardian, the decision of the organisation’s appeals board in March to overturn Senegal’s victory and award the title to Morocco, prompting a legal charade ended by the court of arbitration for sport’s verdict on Tuesday , was a “big joke” that brought Caf and the Afcon into needless disrepute.
“Correcting one injustice with another cannot be considered an acceptable response, either from a sporting or an ethical standpoint,” Sobha said. “Football is founded on core values: fairness, merit and the truth of what happens on the field. Awarding a title outside these principles, even when supported by regulatory provisions, undermines the credibility of the competition and damages the integrity of the game.
“Rather than restoring balance, such a choice risks intensifying frustrations and calls for a deeper reflection on how to safeguard fairness and uphold the honour of African football.”
Managing the huge reputational damage from the crisis over the past 10 months has been arguably the biggest governance test for the five-year Caf presidency of the South African billionaire Patrice Motsepe.
In a frustrated, exasperated moment, he admitted he was “sick and tired” of it all, navigating the treacherous diplomatic minefield of wounded Moroccan and Senegalese feelings, while reiterating his neutrality and belief in the integrity of the judicial process to bring the dispute to a just end.
The Cas resolution of the dispute compels Caf to carry out a desperately needed and long overdue task: the root-and-branch reform of its justice system, particularly the appeals board chaired by the Nigerian judge Roli Harriman.
The Cape Verdean Faustino Varela Monteiro, the board’s vice-chair, is a notable, honourable exception, standing for the correct legal position in his dissenting judgment.
The appeals board needlessly overturned the verdict of Caf’s disciplinary committee, which struck the right balance of upholding the result of the final while imposing fines and bans on the Senegal team for the egregious act of disrupting the match, and in so doing exposed its acute lack of understanding of the critical role it is duty-bound to play in the dispensation of football justice.
“You are right,” says a Caf executive committee member about the need to dissolve the appeals board and reconstitute it with jurists possessing the knowledge needed to restore confidence in the African football justice system.
Ensuring that politically exposed people are no longer members of a reconstituted appeals board is also imperative, if confidence in the impartiality of its verdicts is to be restored. No federation president should have a place on it. The presence of Moez Nasri, the president of the Tunisian Football Federation, strips it of credibility, as Motsepe acknowledged when I pointed this out to him in March.
But the poor quality of Jean-Jacques Ndala Ngambo’s refereeing of the Afcon final and Safari Olivier Kabene’s equally bad chairing of Caf’s referees committee – whose selection of match officials was responsible for the inadequate quality of game management throughout the last tournament – remain the proverbial elephants in the governance room.
When I asked a high-ranking Caf official why Ngambo has not faced a disciplinary hearing for his management of the final, he claimed its hands were tied by the Cas judicial process. That excuse expired on Tuesday.
Ngambo’s decision to allow a restart of the game, after Senegal illegally walked out for about 15 minutes in protest against a penalty awarded to Morocco, was a deeply questionable, some would say unacceptable, use of his discretionary powers, which should have leaned towards a declaration of match abandonment, with Morocco being declared the winners.
That said, the referee’s earlier failure to award Senegal what appeared to be a clear goal, subsequently giving a penalty to Morocco in second-half stoppage time, was the trigger for the chaos.
Ngambo’s lack of fortitude and experience to cope with the demands of an Afcon final is an indictment of the committee that picked the wrong man to handle it. And Kabene is responsible for that. “We have to do a clearout of the referees committee,” says a member of the Caf executive committee.
It is a situation in sharp and sad contrast to the world-class officiating at the 2024 Afcon in Côte d’Ivoire, under the competent general management of the Ivorian Noumandiez Doué, who would be the ideal person to restore sanity.
But after the shabby way he was treated, losing his job while on assignment at the last Championship of African Nations for domestic-based players in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania – the countries staging the 2027 Afcon – it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than it would be to convince him to return to his old job.
With just over eight months to the next Afcon and 20 months to the 2028 tournament, yet to have a designated host, Caf’s governance and organisational challenges are far from over.
The last two Afcons of Motsepe’s presidency, which ends in March 2029, will be decisive in shaping his legacy.

Russia launched scores of drones at energy and civilian targets across Ukraine overnight on Wednesday, killing at least seven people in six regions, authorities said.
The attack involved 112 Shahed, Gerbera and Parodiya decoy drones, of which 88 were shot down or neutralised, Ukraine's air force said.
One person was killed in Bila Tserkva in Kyiv region, where the strike damaged critical infrastructure, an Epicentr shopping centre and a Nova Poshta postal branch, local authorities said.
One person was killed and seven injured in Kharkiv region after a strike hit a minibus on a highway, regional governor Oleh Synehubov said. Two people aged 76 and 69 were killed and another wounded in Sumy region.
Two people were killed in Odesa region on Tuesday evening — a 41-year-old and a 17-year-old — and one person was killed and three wounded in Zhytomyr region. Casualties were also reported in Chernihiv and Donetsk regions.
Russian forces struck a Naftogaz gas production facility in the Poltava region, the acting head of the company Serhiy Fedorenko said.
A fire broke out and the facility suspended operations. "This is not the first such attack and, unfortunately, not the last," Fedorenko said, adding that Russia was deliberately targeting gas production "to deprive Ukrainians of heat in winter."
Energy facilities in the Dnipropetrovsk region were also hit, triggering emergency power cuts across several districts.
A significant number of consumers lost power in Zaporizhzhia region, Zaporizhzhyaoblenergo head Andriy Stasevskyi said. More than 9,000 customers were left without electricity in Odesa region following Tuesday evening's attacks, regional governor Oleh Kiper said.
The energy company DTEK reported a large-scale strike on one of its thermal power plants, causing serious damage and forcing it to stop generating electricity. DTEK did not specify the location, noting it was the third large-scale strike on its plants in November.
Ukrainian drones simultaneously struck three Russian oil refineries overnight, hitting plants in Samara and Rostov regions, according to Ukrainian monitoring sources.
Two refineries in Samara region — the Kuibyshev and Syzran plants, both part of Rosneft — were struck, with fires breaking out at both facilities.
Regional governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev confirmed the attack but did not name the facilities, saying one person was killed, power had been cut in several districts and a number of schools would operate on an adjusted schedule.
Regional authorities said 145 drones were shot down over the Samara region. Euronews could not independently verify these claims.
The Syzran refinery has a processing capacity of 8.5 million tonnes of oil per year and produces petrol, diesel, aviation kerosene, fuel oil and bitumen.
The Kuibyshev refinery has a primary processing capacity of 8.8 million tonnes per year. Ukraine last struck the Syzran plant on 15 September. The Kuibyshev refinery was also struck that month.
The third refinery struck overnight was the Novoshakhtinsk plant in Rostov region. Regional governor Yuri Slyusar confirmed the attack, saying a combined strike of more than 50 drones and missiles lasted six hours before the plant suspended operations.
Russian oil refining volumes have fallen by an estimated 45% since late October, according to analysts.
Ukraine's General Staff also reported overnight strikes on the Savasleyka airbase in Nizhny Novgorod region, which it described as one of Russia's key aviation facilities and the base from which aircraft carrying Kinzhal missiles launch strikes on Ukrainian cities.
According to Kyiv's military, three MiG-31 and two Su-34 aircraft were damaged and would be unable to fly "for some time".
Ukraine destroyed a span of the road section of the Crimean Bridge last week, halting car traffic, though train services have been restored.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the strike was a response to Russian attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure, describing deep strikes inside Russia as "long-range sanctions".
Ukraine attacked the bulk carrier Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday, claiming it transported military cargo. The following day it struck the Russian corvette Merkury in the Libyan port of Benghazi. Zelenskyy confirmed the warship had been sunk.
On Tuesday, Russia's Vladimir Putin threatened Ukraine with retaliation for its strikes on refineries and complained that Kyiv had not heeded calls from US President Donald Trump to halt attacks on oil processing facilities.
Zelenskyy had said Ukraine was prepared to stop striking Russian refineries only if Moscow halted its attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

At least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died since the start of the war in Ukraine in 2022, according to Russian government statistics analysed by the BBC.
The leaked Rosstat data reveal how the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has fundamentally changed mortality patterns in Russia, and show the high cost paid in human life in a war that Vladimir Putin had assumed would last only days but is now almost five years old.
BBC Russian has had access to more than 11 million death records from 2021 to September 2026, after a hack by Belarusian group Cyber Partisans BY and Ukraine's Silent Crow.
Russia's statistics agency admitted to a cyber-attack, but denied any protected information had been leaked.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Wednesday that only Russia's defence ministry could officially report data on losses: "I suggest no other data be taken into account." The defence ministry has not released any official casualty figures for several years.
Together with independent Russian outlet Mediazona, BBC Russian has compared the Rosstat data with its own list of confirmed military deaths, pulled from open sources since the start of the invasion, and it has found matches for 90% of the records.
Military experts estimate that the BBC's list of 290,012 deaths, gleaned from official reports, social media, new memorials and graves, may account for 45-55% of the true death toll, which would range from 527,295 to 644,471.
The records show that 65% of 18 to 24 year-olds in Russia who lost their lives in 2025 died in the war. For those aged 25-34 the number was 59%. Only among 45 to 54 year-olds does cardiovascular disease claim more Russian lives than the conflict.
The data also reveal the extent of losses in specific areas of Ukraine. Some 20,000 Russian soldiers died fighting for control of 10 Ukrainian villages whose combined pre-war population was 12,000.
During the fight for one small village called Andriivka, south of the town of Bakhmut in Donetsk region, 1,122 Russians lost their lives. Before the war 74 people lived there.
Russia does not give public figures for losses sustained since the war began in February 2022. And two years ago Rosstat stopped publishing data of deaths from external causes, which was used to gauge the extent of military losses.
For example, only 70% of deaths we have established of soldiers from the occupied regions of Donetsk and Luhansk in eastern Ukraine who fought in the Russian army were accounted for in the Rosstat files.
Overall, the Rosstat dataset confirms the trends that we have observed with our own count.
Ukrainian losses were last put at about 50,000 by President Volodymyr Zelensky in July 2026, but another list based on open sources by the anonymous UA Losses website puts the figure at 115,952.
The Rosstat dataset contains no names but does include ages, places of residence, places of death and also circumstances of death.
We have filtered the records first by location, leaving only Ukraine as well as Russian border regions that saw incursions by the Ukrainian army.
Next, we identified 425,174 entries explicitly indicating a military-related cause of death, such as explosions or shrapnel during combat operations.
As this count could include civilians, we filtered out women as well as men outside the 18-65 age group. And if someone lived and died in the four Ukrainian regions occupied by Russia, we excluded them as a possible civilian – unless he had a record of military service attached to his entry.
Another 14,093 entries were identified by looking at employment, and 51,067 were recorded in the database as deceased on the basis of a court ruling. This often happens when a soldier goes missing in a combat zone for more than six months and their body has not been recovered.
Again, we filtered out civilians by only counting deaths in the war zones in Ukraine and Russia.
According to BBC Russian's analysis of the leaked files, in the first year of the war the average age of those killed was 34. By 2025, as prisoners and contract soldiers entered the ranks, it had risen to 40 (38 according to our own list).
Some of Russia's poorest regions in Eastern Siberia account for a disproportionately large share of the losses. Men from Tyva, Buryatia and Zabaykalsky Krai are 20-25 times more likely to die in the war than residents of the biggest cities of Moscow and St Petersburg.
In most regions, the distribution of deaths based on Rosstat data differs from that in the BBC's list by just a few tenths of a percentage point.
At least 5,017 foreigners are among those who died fighting for Russia, according to our analysis of the Rosstat files, including 1,031 Uzbeks and 720 Tajiks. We have left out Ukrainians from this count to avoid including civilians.
This is a conservative estimate as dual nationals are listed as Russians in the database, and there is no reference to North Koreans who died repelling the Ukrainian incursion into Russia in 2024.
The BBC identified 2,304 North Korean soldiers who died there by analysing satellite imagery and official photographs of a newly built memorial in Pyongyang.
The leaked Russian statistics may not be complete but taken in conjunction with BBC Russian's own work they are significant.
In the context of a war that has lasted four years and 10 months, these are high numbers for Russia, when compared with the Soviet war in Afghanistan that ended in 1989.
In that 10-year war, an estimated 15,000 Red Army troops died, and an estimated one million civilians were killed.

Chen Jining, regarded as a contender for higher office, becomes the fourth member of China’s elite politburo to be investigated since 2025
China has launched an investigation into Shanghai’s Communist party chief Chen Jining, a member of the country’s elite politburo, the state-run Xinhua news agency unexpectedly announced on Tuesday, marking the fourth member of the top leadership ⁠body to be probed since ⁠2025.
China’s anti-graft watchdog is investigating ​Chen for “suspected severe violations of discipline and laws”, Xinhua said, using a common euphemism for corruption.
For Chinese officials, especially those of Chen’s ⁠rank, the public announcement of an investigation by the central commission for discipline inspection generally signals their eventual political downfall.
The investigation marks a further escalation in President Xi Jinping’s widening anti-graft campaign, which has thinned the party’s senior leadership ranks and depleted the military’s top command.
Before the announcement of the Chen probe, three politburo members from the once 24-member body formed in 2022 – He Weidong, Zhang ⁠Youxia and Ma Xingrui – had already been purged .
Chen, 62, had an unusual rise through China’s official ranks. ​An environmental scientist by training, he earned a doctorate from Imperial ‌College London and rose through China’s elite Tsinghua ‌University to become its president.
He entered government as China’s environmental protection minister in 2015 – just as Xi was elevating pollution control and ecological protection as ‌policy priorities – before becoming mayor of Beijing. He joined the politburo in 2022 and was named party boss of Shanghai, China’s financial hub.
He has long been viewed as a political star and a plausible contender for higher national office. The investigation into him took analysts by surprise.
The hashtag “Chen Jining under investigation” had amassed about 240m views on the Chinese microblogging platform Weibo by Wednesday morning, with many users saying they were “shocked” and “stunned” in comments under state media posts.
“This is arguably the biggest political news to come out of China in a few years,” Taisu Zhang, a professor at Yale Law School specialising in contemporary Chinese law and politics, wrote on X.
Zhang pointed to Chen’s status as a rising political star who had been seen as “a near-lock for the politburo Standing Committee”, China’s highest political decision-making body.
At a gathering of leaders last month, the ruling Communist party pledged to keep waging indefinitely its high-pressure anti-corruption campaign , which has ensnared millions within ‌China’s vast bureaucracy and has seen hundreds of top officials purged , including those once thought untouchable.
Xi had called on the party to “turn the blade inward” and unleash a revolution on itself and eradicate “viruses and impurities” that corrode its health. The party views ​the drive as essential to ensuring its long-term survival.
“No matter who they are, how high their position, or how great their contributions, anyone who engages in corruption will surely receive no leniency,” Xi said in January.
Chen’s unexpected probe “sends a signal that there’s no letting up in the anti-corruption drive and the party’s ‘self-revolution,’” said China expert Jean Christopher Mittelstaedt of the University of Zurich.
The Shanghai party secretary post is one of China’s most prestigious provincial-level positions and has often served as a springboard to top leadership roles.
Xi himself briefly served as Shanghai’s party boss in 2007 before joining the politburo’s standing committee, the country’s highest decision-making body.
“Chen Jining is no ordinary fallen official … [He is] an exemplar of someone who rose from the specialised field of environmental protection to the pinnacle of political power,” Mao Shoulong, a professor of public administration and policy at Renmin University of China, wrote in a commentary on WeChat.
“His downfall, therefore, is not merely that of an individual, but of an entire type of official, a model of political advancement, and a set of assumptions about the relationship between technology and politics, expertise and power, and competence and loyalty,” Mao wrote.
Shanghai’s senior party leadership pledged loyalty to Beijing and understanding of the need to “see things through ⁠to the end” ⁠after Chen ​was put under investigation, the financial hub’s official paper said on Wednesday.

Australia and the Solomon Islands have signed a new treaty on security and economics
The Solomon Islands has signed a "historic" treaty with Australia, after reportedly telling China it was ending a controversial security pact signed in 2022.
At a press conference in Canberra on Wednesday, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Solomon Islands counterpart Matthew Wale said the new treaty would ensure that Australia was the Pacific nation's "security partner of choice".
In 2022 the Solomon Islands, then under the leadership of now-Opposition Leader Manasseh Sogavare, signed a security and policing pact with Beijing .
There were fears the pact gave China a crucial military and strategic foothold in the Pacific amid a battle for influence in the region with the US.
On Tuesday, Australian media outlets reported that Honiara had told Beijing it would not renew the pact, understood to be expiring in April 2027.
Wale told reporters on Wednesday there were "ongoing discussions" with China but he was "unable to talk about" the pact, because of a non-disclosure agreement.
He said the treaty with Australia provided a reset after several years in which the Solomon Islands had been a point of "uncertainty and doubt in the region".
Albanese said the treaty would strengthen the two countries' security partnership.
"Backing our Pacific neighbours is an investment in Australia's own security and our own prosperity."
"We'll do that in a way that completely respects Solomon Islands sovereignty and its right to make its own decisions."
On Tuesday China's foreign ministry spokesman, Guo Jiukan, did not confirm or deny that the pact had been terminated.
"There is no element of geopolitical rivalry or bloc confrontation in cooperation between China and Pacific island countries, including the Solomon Islands," Guo said.
The pact was never publicly released, but leaked excerpts revealed it gave China extensive involvement in security and policing including deploying its own officers to the Solomon Islands, and allowed it to establish a quasi military base.
It was a "massive coup" for Beijing, said Lowy Institute Research Fellow, Dr Connor Graham, but its unprecedented scale sparked alarm in the Pacific and the West.
Wednesday's treaty had delivered "an enormous win for Canberra", and "closes the loop" on a series of security deals Canberra signed with Pacific nations in the wake of the Solomons-China pact.
"That [China pact] was the thing that put fear in the hearts of diplomats in Washington and Canberra," he told the BBC.
William Yang, the International Crisis Group's Senior Analyst for North East Asia, said the end of China's "flagship" Pacific deal and the signing of the new treaty also reaffirmed the Pacific's "longstanding consensus-based decision-making model, especially in the security space".
Under the new treaty, the Solomon Islands commits to prior consultation with Australia on critical infrastructure and to ensure any security cooperations are with Pacific Islands Forum members. China is a dialogue partner but not a member of the forum.
Honiara also commits to its sensitive infrastructure remaining "free from militarisation, any form of foreign interference or unauthorised access", and to not permit its territory to be used for any foreign military or security base.
The Solomons will receive support for its free education system and sports programs, improved visa arrangements, and support for the expansion of affordable and renewable energy and infrastructure development.
Earlier this week the ABC reported the package promised more than A$980m (£460.7m, $648,000) in additional funding, citing leaked text messages. The BBC has not independently verified the text messages.
Wale visited Australia to sign the treaty, accompanied by two dozen Solomons MPs. He and Albanese said the size of the delegation demonstrated that the treaty had strong support from the country's parliament, after years of political instability - largely driven by disagreement over the country's relationship with China .

Solomon Islands will have to consult Canberra before making new security or infrastructure deals under new pact.
Solomon Islands and Australia have signed a sweeping treaty affirming that the small Pacific country will allow no foreign military bases on its territory.
The deal, signed on Wednesday, is seen as a blow to the regional ambitions of China, which had been moving closer to the Solomon Islands for years.
“Solomon Islands has been for a number of years a source of uncertainty and doubt in the region. Those days are gone,” Prime Minister Matthew Wale told journalists alongside his Australian counterpart Anthony Albanese.
The treaty establishes Australia as the island nation’s “primary security partner” and will see Canberra provide 740 million Australian dollars ($490m) over the next 10 years to fund free education and other programmes in Solomon Islands. Solomon Islands has a gross domestic product (GDP) of $1.75bn, according to the World Bank.
In exchange, Solomon Islands will allow no foreign military or security bases on its soil, and the country’s “sensitive” infrastructure will “remain free from militarisation, foreign interference and unauthorised access”.
That includes ports, airports, energy and telecommunications, as well as road and bridge construction – areas China has dominated in the islands through its Belt and Road Initiative. The deal will not apply retroactively.
Solomon Islands will also have to consult Australia before making deals involving its critical infrastructure or security cooperation unless it is with members of the Pacific Islands Forum regional bloc, Albanese said.
Since being elected in May, Wale has upended Solomon Islands’ diplomatic moves towards China and realigned with Australia and the United States.
Asked about reports he had ended a secretive security pact with Beijing, Wale told journalists that discussions with China were “ongoing”.
China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs did not confirm whether the deal had been scrapped, but warned that the new agreement with Australia “should not target any third party”.
This is the latest in a string of similar deals Australia has struck with Pacific states, including Papua New Guinea , Vanuatu and Fiji .

Jude Bellingham admits he had ‘no idea’ what he’d done after scoring a goal that drew comparisons with Zinadine Zidane.
Real Madrid star Jude Bellingham has brushed aside comparisons with football great Zinedine Zidane following his sensational goal against PSV in the Champions League.
The England international came on at half-time with Los Blancos trailing and inspired a sensational second-half display, including a magnificent effort from distance, at the Santiago Bernabeu on Tuesday.
Bellingham said he “did not know” how he scored his brilliant goal, flicking the ball up on the edge of the box and slicing a stunning effort inside the far post.
Having seen an acrobatic volley blocked minutes earlier, the England midfielder controlled Kylian Mbappe’s pass with two touches in the air and curled a superb shot into ⁠⁠the far corner from well outside the area.
“I have no idea what I did,” Bellingham told RMTV. “I had the ball in a good position and thought about shooting.”
The 23-year-old, upon joining Real Madrid, took Zidane’s number five shirt in “homage” to the Frenchman, whom he admired, and some have compared his goal to a Zidane-style strike.
“I do things that you guys think are similar to Zidane, but he was much better than me,” Bellingham told reporters.
Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho hailed Bellingham’s game-changing display as the midfielder gave Mourinho credit for helping him find arguably the best form he has enjoyed at Madrid in recent weeks, with Los Blancos winning a 10th straight match, but the coach said the midfielder only had himself to thank.
“I think the main figure responsible for what Jude is today is Jude, and his teammates. I try to help a little,” said the Portuguese coach.
“He’s an absolutely extraordinary player who has everything – he has physicality, he has technique, he has tactical understanding of the game, he has ambition, he has absolutely everything and today, obviously not by himself, but he changed the direction of the match.”
“He’s an absolutely extraordinary player and for me, without any doubt, the best midfielder in the world,” Mourinho said.
Madrid’s victory over the Dutch champions maintained their 100 percent start to the league phase, in which they are provisional leaders.
Mourinho reiterated his view that it was a “scandal” that Bellingham was not ranked in the top 10 players in the world at this year’s Ballon d’Or ceremony.

The US military is set to detonate 68 barrels containing nearly 9,500lb of lead azide in Iowa at 10am Eastern time on Wednesday.
As the Guardian has previously reported , the army has changed the date three times after an outpouring of public concern about potential health and environmental effects.
Nearly 400 people live in Middletown, a small town in south-eastern Iowa , where the plant is situated. The army has warned that the blast could release a plume of toxic lead dust extending up to 100 miles northeast, possibly reaching cities such as Wapello and New Boston, Illinois.
Last week, Iowa governor Kim Reynolds, a Republican, activated the state emergency management office, and the state created a website for information about the detonation.
Stick with us as we bring you the latest news from this planned detonation.
In a video on Wednesday, the Assistant Secretary of the Army explained the decision behind the operation.
“The choice that we faced here was between a spontaneous, uncontrolled detonation of dangerous material or a controlled detonation where we could choose the time, and place to optimize the conditions and deliver the best result not just for our operations, but for the safety of the public and the surrounding communities” the secretary, Jordan Gillis, said.
The United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has activated an emergency response to support the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services to “provide accurate public health communication and technical assistance to our state and federal partners.”
In a statement, the CDC said that at the request of the state of Iowa , it will support the state’s health department to develop “recommendations to help protect people from potential exposure to lead and air pollution” and in preparing to support the state with any “any post-event community health assessment needs.”
The CDC also said that it was “activating a multidisciplinary team with expertise in toxicology, communications, and public health emergency response.”
The organization on Tuesday urged residents to “pay attention to alerts related to the detonation”, and to stay indoors or evacuate “if you are in the evacuation zone, until state officials indicate that the air is safe to return home.”
They told residents to “close all doors and windows in your home” and to “seal any gaps to prevent outdoor air from coming indoors”.
We’re getting the latest images from the newswires from towns around the Iowa army site where the lead azide detonation is planned for today:
NASA has mobilized “specialized research aircraft, space-based observation capabilities, and scientific personnel” to support efforts at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Iowa, the agency said.
“NASA stands ready to bring its unique capabilities and world-class scientific expertise to bear whenever called upon in service of the nation and the American people” the agency said in a statement .

Chen is the fourth high-ranking Politburo member to be pushed out in two years.
The Chinese Communist Party has launched investigations into the party’s Shanghai secretary Chen Jining for alleged “serious violations of discipline and law” – usually code for corruption.
The anticorruption watchdog, the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, announced the probe in a brief statement on Tuesday, according to Xinhua News Agency, but did not give more details.
It comes amid widespread purges in the Political Bureau, one of the top bodies of the CCP, as the party prepares for its next congress in the second half of 2027, where President Xi Jinping is expected to clinch his fourth five-year term.
Xi, who has pushed greater party discipline and anticorruption, has for years pursued a long, intense purge on a scale not seen since the rule of Mao Zedong, experts say.
The Shanghai Communist Party’s leaders have backed the move, with its standing committee stating it firmly supported the decision to investigate Chen and that it showed Beijing’s determination to continue its anticorruption campaign.
“The takedown again shows that Xi Jinping’s anticorruption campaign has no limits,” Mingda Qiu, a senior analyst at Eurasia Group, told The Associated Press news agency. “The pattern is unprecedented.” Here’s what we know:
Chen, 62, joined the CCP as a 20-year-old environmental engineering student at the highly-rated Tsinghua University. After spending a decade researching in the United Kingdom, the scientist and academic returned to Tsinghua, where he was eventually appointed one of its youngest presidents in 2012.
He went on to serve as the Minister of Environmental Protection from 2015 to 2017, and led efforts to cut pollution in Beijing. He was later appointed Mayor of Beijing in 2018.
In 2022, he was appointed party secretary of Shanghai, the country’s financial hub, amid Xi’s push to install people with strong scientific backgrounds in key roles.
Chen was widely seen as Xi’s protege. His post is usually seen as a stepping stone to party leadership; President Xi previously held the position of Shanghai Party Secretary in 2007.
Chen hosted some of China’s most prominent diplomatic visitors, including former US Secretary of State Antony Blinken, former British Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.
He led the opening ceremony of the World AI Conference held earlier this year in Shanghai.
Other senior party officials have been purged in recent months, especially in the military.
The military shakeups and wider purge are part of Xi’s years-long anticorruption drive that has seen hundreds of senior and junior government officials investigated, prosecuted or dismissed since Xi first came to power in 2012.
Analysts believe the purges are designed to reform the military and to ensure unwavering loyalty to Xi.
Some military expulsions have been linked to suspicions of political divergence. Official sources, for example, described additional allegations against He Weidong, the former vice chairman of the military commission, as being a “loss of chastity,” a rare phrase which, in CCP speak, refers to political disloyalty and ideological collapse.
The takedowns reveal how Chinese politics often depends on shifting circumstances, with even officials possessing the qualifications Xi wants being vulnerable to removal, said Joseph Torigian, a professor at the Washington-based American University.
“On paper,” they appear to be “individuals Xi would appreciate,” Torigian told the AP. But afterwards, “we could easily come up with hypotheses for why he got rid of them”.

Derya Uluğ, ağustos ayında muhabirlerin sorularını yanıtlarken düğün planlarını da paylaşmıştı. Şarkıcı, 'Allah'tan bir mani olmazsa 2027 yılına evli olarak gireceğiz. Yılbaşından önce, önümüzdeki 4 ay içerisinde sade, sevdiklerimiz ve ailemizle birlikte olacağımız mutlu bir akşam hayal ediyoruz' demişti.
Bu planın ardından çiftin 25 Kasım'da nikah masasına oturması bekleniyor. Düğün hazırlıkları sürerken sade ve samimi bir organizasyon planlandığı ifade ediliyor.

Geceden paylaşım yapan isimler arasında şarkıcı Ece Seçkin de vardı. Hamile olan Seçkin, kına gecesinden bir kareyi sosyal medya hesabından paylaştı.

Englishman hailed by teammates and manager Mourinho after coming on to completely change Champions League game against PSV Eindhoven
“I t was one of those moments when you’re just: ‘Wow.’” Bernardo Silva had a good view of Jude Bellingham scoring the goal, the golazo , that put Real Madrid into the lead and the Bernabéu on its feet, shock giving way to song, naa, naa, naa, na-na-na-naa, na-na-na-naa ringing round again. “I have no idea what I did,” the Englishman said afterwards. What he did was turn all Le Tissier. Lifting the ball with his left, raising it with his right, twisting and not letting it drop, he sent it arching from the outside of his boot into the far corner, something straight out of the 90s.
“I just kind of hit it,” Bellingham reckoned; not wanting to hit it too hard, it had gone “looping”, “stabbing”, he said. “Normally [my goals are] a lot closer, aren’t they? I was a bit surprised, honestly. Normally from there I’m looking to see who is an option to play it through to, but it popped up nicely. It was nice.” Nice? It was, Silva said, “special”. A “work of art” Marca called it. The presenter on one radio station claimed it was the best goal he had ever seen, and it wasn’t just him; wasn’t just the goal, either.
“I thought, maybe wrongly, that we could win without Bellingham,” José Mourinho admitted afterwards. The Englishman had what Madrid’s manager called an “almost injury” but at half-time, with Madrid a goal down against PSV Eindhoven and thankful it was just one, he had decided that he had to go on anyway. He had also given them what Bellingham called a “kick up the backside we needed”. Fifteen minutes later, Bellingham was standing there, arms wide. Madrid were 2-1 up; by the end it was 5-1, Bellingham setting Vinícius Júnior free for the fifth.
He had been “absolutely devastating”, Mourinho said. Some injury: everywhere and everything, he had transformed them all, Madrid growing in what El País called “the burning light of Bellingham’s sun”. Marca led on: “Jude resuscitates Real Madrid .” “Bellingham stages a festival,” said AS, Tomas Roncero calling him “the Colossus of Stourbridge”. He had been Polyphemus, El Mundo reckoned. The veteran journalist Alfredo Relano described him as the closest thing to Alfredo Di Stefano in “how he runs the game, spreading optimism to everyone”.
Then there was Zinedine Zidane, whose number he has inherited and with whom the comparisons were everywhere. During the game on Tuesday night he had “Zidaned”, Marca said and so did pretty much everyone else. After the game, the same name was put to him. “It’s a bit much that, eh,” Bellingham replied. “Zidane is much better than me, much more elegant. He is my idol.”
Actually, Bellingham has matched Zidane for leagues and Champions Leagues at Real Madrid already. And, as Jorge Valdano was swift to point out, it’s not just that he might be the best midfielder in the world right now; it’s that he’s still just 23. In theory, there’s a decade more of this; in theory, Bellingham’s prime is still to come.
Set to extend his contract to 2031 in the coming days, these are Bellingham’s best days. At the start of the season Mourinho had said: “He’s a No 10. He can’t play … well, he can play as a 6 or an 8, but then you lose him being closer to goal and I like that Jude.” Yet while there has been a shift this can still feel like the Jude that is everywhere too, the kid who was once handed the No 22 shirt because he was a 10, an 8 and a 4 all together , a player who can’t be stopped as he strides towards the area, opponents flying off him when he turns, like a catherine wheel spinning through midfield.
“He’s very special,” Silva told TNT. “He is a player that can create something very different at any moment like today. Physically he is very strong, the way he keeps the ball, the way he allows us to attack, the way he drives with the ball. He is good at everything. He is a complete player.”
Mourinho described him as “an extraordinary player”. He said: “Jude has everything: the physique, the technical ability, the understanding of the play, vision … everything. He is the best midfielder in the world. He changed the game. He is a natural leader, he makes huge demands of himself: you see that every day in the way he trains. He doesn’t hide his frustration when things don’t go well but he combats that with work, by putting the machine to work.”
Unleashed and undroppable, he has seven goals and five assists, as if it is even about that, however absurd the latest one was. Few, if any, footballers are playing better anywhere. Even if asked about the Ballon d’Or – yes, already – Bellingham replied that he doesn’t care about that, claiming that’s a journalists’ thing.
“I have a bit more experience now: there’s the coach, the staff, the confidence I have from the World Cup,” he said, speaking to the media in English and Spanish. “My Spanish is getting better, although I get a bit nervous with you. It’s easier in the changing room where I can say bad words. I’m loving it here. For English players, it’s such a good thing to play abroad.”

Whether through deception or desperation, Indians continue to be drawn into Russia's war in Ukraine. What can New Delhi do to protect its citizens from ending up fighting in Ukraine?
Gurpreet Singh Randhawa, a 40-year-old from Jalandhar in India's northern Punjab state, said he traveled to Russia for work after responding to a Facebook advertisement for a driving job at a garment factory.
But instead of finding work as a driver, he was sent to fight in Ukraine for the Russian armed forces .
After escaping from his unit, he surrendered to Ukrainian forces in November. He is now being held as a prisoner of war.
In an interview with Ukrainian YouTuber Volodymyr Zolkin, Randhawa described how, after arriving in Russia, he was taken to a military facility, made to sign a contract and sent for training. He said they confiscated his passport and phone. His account has not been independently verified.
He is the second Indian national known to have escaped the Russian military. Sahil Majothi, a 23-year-old from Gujarat, surrendered to Ukrainian forces in October 2025. He had joined the Russian military while serving a prison sentence in Russia, reportedly believing that military service would help him secure his release.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
The cases underline how little has changed since Prime Minister Narendra Modi raised the issue with Russian President Vladimir Putin during his visit to Moscow in July 2024 .
At the time, Putin assured him that Indians who were misled into joining the Russian army would be discharged. But the recruitment of Indians has continued.
In an October filing before the Supreme Court, India's Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said approximately 267 Indians have joined the Russian armed forces since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine .
Of these, 139 were discharged and 51 were killed. The whereabouts of the 77 others were unknown. Russian authorities have confirmed that seven of them are missing.
The problem extends beyond Indians who travel to Russia seeking civilian employment, only to find themselves exposed to recruitment networks and the dangers of a war zone.
The MEA has also highlighted cases of Indians knowingly enlisting in the Russian military for the supposed financial benefits on offer, believing they could later secure release through government intervention.
Some had also approached Indian authorities to renounce their citizenship and obtain Russian passports. "This is a dangerous path and is strongly discouraged by the government," the ministry said.
Former diplomat Anil Trigunayat said the growing movement of Indian workers to Russia presents both economic opportunities and new challenges for their protection.
"Inadequate oversight of recruitment networks could leave vulnerable workers exposed to exploitation," Trigunayat told DW.
He said Indian workers were often burdened by substantial recruitment fees and continued deductions from their salaries by intermediaries.
"Some of them had paid between 300,000 to 500,000 Indian rupees [$5,400 /€4,900] to Indian recruitment agents, and even while working in Russia, more than 30% of their agreed monthly salary was taken away by local and foreign agents," Trigunayat said.
The former diplomat added that some Indians who had overstayed their visas in Russia were particularly vulnerable. Military service was allegedly offered to earn substantial wages and regularize their immigration status.
Mohammad Sufiyan, from Hyderabad in the southern state of Telangana, said he was lured to Russia under false pretences and forced into active combat in Ukraine.
He had traveled abroad in search of employment and a better livelihood, but ended up in a war zone. He has since returned home to India .
"Many people are duped. Some decide it is better to seek citizenship than come back to India. It's a tough life, and people will go to any lengths to get some sort of employment," Sufiyan told DW.
Sufiyan's experience points to the economic desperation that makes such offers attractive, even when they carry the risk of being caught up in a war.
Rajan Kumar, a professor at the Centre for Russian and Central Asian Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University's School of International Studies, said some Indians who traveled to Russia for work could find themselves caught up in the fighting without having joined the military.
"Some of them, they don't join the army, but they end up in the army region. They're caught in the crossfire," Kumar told DW.
He said India was negotiating with Moscow to secure the return of its citizens caught up in such situations. "Russia is very cooperative so far," he said.
India has been pressing Russia to take action, but the issue persists.
The recruitment efforts reflect Russia's need for more manpower for its nearly five-year war in Ukraine , and the limited influence New Delhi can exert over Moscow, despite the close political relationship between the two countries.
Mohsin Raza Khan, a professor at the Jindal School of International Affairs, told DW that Putin 's need to sustain the war effort was taking precedence over the concerns of a strategic partner.
He points out that the Russian president was reluctant to impose another mobilization on his own population for fear of domestic unrest.
"In these circumstances, sustaining the war effort appears to take precedence over concerns raised by India. Neither Modi nor New Delhi has sufficient leverage to change that," said Khan.
Khan also said the willingness of some Indians to enlist, and even consider giving up their citizenship, is down to the lack of decent employment opportunities at home.
"For young, educated men without contacts or connections, the chances of respectable employment are so low that the risks of a high casualty war are preferable," he said.

Olay, 21 Kasım’da İzmit ilçesi Yeşilova Mahallesi'nde meydana geldi. Kız çocuğunun sokakta sürdüğü bisiklet, yol kenarında duran otomobile sürttü.
Durumu fark edip otomobilden inen erkek sürücü, kızın bisikletini aldı. Çocuğa bağıran ismi öğrenilemeyen sürücü, ailesini çağırmasını istedi.
Çevredekilerin ve esnafın uyarılarına rağmen tepkisini sürdüren sürücüden korkan kız, annesine haber vermek için eve gitti. Bu sırada otomobilden inen ve sürücünün annesi olduğu öğrenilen kadın, çocuğun bisikletini birkaç kez kaldırıp yere vurarak kırdı.
Daha sonra kız çocuğu da annesiyle olay yerine gelince taraflar arasında tartışma çıktı.
Yaşananlar, bir iş yerinin güvenlik kamerasına yansıdı. Görüntülerin haberleştirilmesinin ardından kimliklerini belirlenen anne ve oğlunun polis merkezinde ifadeleri alındı. Anne-oğul daha sonra serbest bırakıldı. Tarafların birbirinden şikayetçi olmadıkları belirtildi.

Sağlam ile birlikte çektiği videoyu da sanal medya hesabından paylaşan Akalın, "Geldim kızı buldum. Şimdi bisikleti almaya gidiyoruz" dedi.

Otomobil almak isteyenler için kredi kartı faizleri aşağı çekildi. Yüksek limitli kartı olanlar, galeri veya sıfır araç bayilerinden yüzde 4,25 yerine yüzde 4,08 aylık faizle taksitli araç alabilecek. Kartla alımda ne ipotek ne de kredi başvurusu gerekiyor, ancak 500 bin TL'lik bir araç 12 ayda yaklaşık 689 bin TL'ye çıkıyor.
Merkez Bankası 'nın kredi kartı faizlerinde kullanılan referans oranı yüzde 3,11'den 2,94'e çekmesi, 1 Aralık 2026'dan itibaren kartlara yansıyacak. Kademeler kartın dönem borcuna göre belirleniyor. Dönem borcu 180 bin TL'nin üzerinde olan kartlarda azami akdi faiz yüzde 4,25'ten 4,08'e, azami gecikme faizi ise yüzde 4,55'ten 4,38'e düşecek.
Dönem borcu 30 bin ile 180 bin TL arasındaki kartlarda oran yüzde 3,75'ten 3,58'e iniyor. Aracın bedeli kartla ödendiğinde borç 180 bin TL'yi aşıyorsa en yüksek kademe devreye giriyor. Yüksek limitli kartı olanlar da galeri veya sıfır araç bayilerinden bu yeni oranla taksitli araç alabilecek.
Kredi çekerek araç almak isteyenleri ise sınırlar bekliyor. 400 bin TL ve altındaki araçlarda azami vade 48 ay, 400 bin ile 800 bin TL arasında 36 ay, 800 bin ile 1 milyon 200 bin TL arasında 24 ay, 1 milyon 200 bin ile 2 milyon TL arasında ise 12 ay. Kredinin araç değerine oranı da aynı kademelerde yüzde 70, yüzde 50, yüzde 30 ve yüzde 20 ile sınırlı.
Yani 1 milyon TL'lik bir araç için en fazla yüzde 30'u, 300 bin TL kredi çıkabiliyor. İhtiyaç kredisinde de benzer bir tablo var: 125 bin TL ve altında en fazla 36 ay, 125 bin 1 TL ile 250 bin TL arasında 24 ay, 250 bin TL ve üzerinde 12 ay vade uygulanıyor.
NTV'nin hesabına göre aracın tamamı kartla alınır ve 12 ay vade seçilirse 500 bin TL'lik araç için aylık ödeme 57.384 TL oluyor. Toplam faiz 188.608 TL tutuyor, yani faiz yükü araç bedelinin yaklaşık yüzde 38'ine denk geliyor.
1 milyon TL'lik araçta aylık taksit 114.768 TL, toplam faiz 377.216 TL, geri ödeme ise yaklaşık 1 milyon 377 bin TL. 2 milyon TL'lik araçta ise aylık 229.536 TL ödeniyor; 754.433 TL faizle birlikte geri ödeme yaklaşık 2 milyon 754 bin TL'ye ulaşıyor.
Bazı galericiler ve bayiler kredi kartına taksitli araç satışı yapıyor. Üstelik bir miktar peşinat verip kalan tutarı taksitlendirmek de mümkün. Bu durumda taşıt kredisindeki vade ve kredi oranı sınırları devreye girmiyor.
Örnek olarak 1 milyon TL'lik bir ikinci el aracın yarısı peşin ödeniyor, kalan 500 bin TL karta yüklenip 12 aya bölünüyor. Aylık ödeme 57.384 TL'de kalıyor ve 1 milyon TL'lik araç bu şekilde alınmış oluyor. Taksit sayısı ve komisyon gibi koşullar ise satıcıdan satıcıya değişebiliyor.
Kartla alımın en dikkat çeken yanı, araca kredi çekilmediği için üzerinde ipotek bulunmaması. Bu yüzden araç istenen an satılıp nakde çevrilebiliyor; taşıt kredisinde olduğu gibi bir kısıtlama yok.
Düşen kredi kartı faizleri ise 1 Aralık'ta yürürlüğe giriyor.

İstanbul Ticaret Odası ( İTO ) Başkanı Şekib Avdagiç, yazılı açıklamasında konut kredilerindeki gevşemeyi, kredi kartı ve kredili mevduat hesabı (KMH) faizlerinde açıklanan indirimi olumlu karşıladıklarını belirtti.
Kredi kartı faiz indiriminin 1 Aralık’ta yürürlüğe gireceğini hatırlatan Avdagiç, benzer adımların ticari kredilerde de atılmasının reel sektörü destekleyeceğini ifade etti.
“İşletmelerimiz ticari kredilerde somut indirimler bekliyor” diyen Avdagiç, finansman koşullarındaki iyileşmenin üretim ve arz kapasitesini artırarak fiyatlar üzerindeki baskıyı hafifletebileceğini söyledi.
Avdagiç, politika faizi yüzde 36’ya gerilerken ticari kredi faizlerinin bu seviyenin belirgin şekilde üzerinde kaldığını, bu kredilerdeki faiz düşüşünün de dalgalı ve sınırlı seyrettiğini kaydetti. Avdagiç, İTO üyelerinin bankaların uyguladığı komisyon ve dosya masraflarının finansman maliyetlerini artırdığını bildirdiğini aktardı.
Merkez Bankasının 11 Kasım’da KOBİ kredilerinde büyüme sınırını yüzde 5’ten yüzde 5,5’e yükseltmesini olumlu bulduklarını belirten Avdagiç, sınırın daha da artırılmasının ve üretim, ihracat ve yatırım kredilerinin sınır dışında tutulmasının finansmana erişimi kolaylaştıracağını söyledi.
Avdagiç, iş dünyasının 2027’ye daha elverişli finansman koşullarıyla girmesinin üretim, istihdam ve yatırımı destekleyeceğini ifade etti.

Nazmi Sağlam ile çektiği videoyu sosyal medya hesabından paylaşan şarkıcı, "Geldim kızı buldum. Şimdi bisikleti almaya gidiyoruz" ifadelerini kullandı.
Videoda küçük kızın dedesine birden fazla bisiklet gönderileceğini söylediği için tepki gösteren Akalın, "Kaç tane bisiklet gelecek dedin niye öyle diyorsun ki? Bırak yollasınlar bisikletleri" dedi. Nazmi Sağlam ise "Gerek yok ki. Gerekmez bisiklet. Türkiye'mize teşekkür ediyoruz" sözleriyle karşılık verdi.
Olay, 21 Kasım'da İzmit Yeşilova Mahallesi'nde yaşandı. İddiaya göre küçük kızın bisikleti sokakta otomobile sürtünce sürücü araçtan inerek bisikleti aldı ve çocuğa ailesini çağırmasını söyledi. Sürücüden korkan kız annesine haber vermek için eve gitti.
Bu sırada sürücünün annesi olduğu belirtilen kadın, bisikleti birkaç kez kaldırıp yere vurarak kırdı. Kızın annesiyle olay yerine gelmesi üzerine taraflar arasında tartışma yaşandı. O anlar bir iş yerinin güvenlik kamerasıyla kaydedildi.
Görüntülerin haberleştirilmesi üzerine kimlikleri belirlenen anne ve oğlunun polis merkezinde ifadeleri alındı. İfadelerinin ardından serbest bırakılan tarafların birbirlerinden şikayetçi olmadıkları belirtildi.

İstanbul Ticaret Odası ( İTO ) Başkanı Şekib Avdagiç yaptığı yazılı açıklamada, 1 Aralık'ta yürürlüğe girecek kredi kartı faizi indiriminin ardından, finansal koşullardaki iyileşmenin ticari kredilerle devam etmesinin reel sektöre önemli katkı sağlayacağına inandıklarını ifade etti.
Ticari kredilerde sağlanacak rahatlamanın, üretim ve arz kapasitesini destekleyerek fiyatlar üzerindeki baskının hafiflemesine ve enflasyonla mücadeleye de katkı vereceğini belirten Avdagiç, "Geçen hafta konut kredilerindeki gevşeme ve dün de kredi kartı faizlerinde yapılan indirimi en makul bir süre içinde ticari kredilerin de izlemesi reel sektör için yararlı olacaktır. Konut kredisi ve kredi kartı adımlarını ticari krediler için de bekliyoruz." değerlendirmesinde bulundu.
Avdagiç, son dönemde finansal koşulların iyileştirilmesi yönünde başlayan sürecin ticari kredilerde de hissedilir bir rahatlamayla devam etmesinin reel sektöre önemli katkı sağlayacağına inandıklarını kaydetti.
Konut kredisi ve kredi kartı faizlerine ilişkin adımlara değinen Avdagiç, şu ifadeleri kullandı:
"Geçen hafta konut kredilerinde atılan gevşeme adımını, dün de kredi kartı ve kredili mevduat hesabı (KMH) faizlerinde açıklanan indirimi olumlu karşılıyoruz. Üretimin, istihdamın ve ihracatın yükünü taşıyan ticari kredilerde de benzer bir rahatlama sağlanması, İTO üyesi firmalarımızın beklenti ve talepleri arasında ön sırada yer alıyor. İşletmelerimiz ticari kredilerde somut indirimler bekliyor. Merkez Bankasının da vurguladığı gibi, arz yönlü iyileşme dezenflasyonu daha görünür kılacaktır."
İTO Başkanı Avdagiç, politika faizinin yüzde 36'ya inmiş olmasına rağmen ticari kredi faizlerinin hala bu seviyenin belirgin şekilde üzerinde seyrettiğini, ticari kredi faizlerindeki düşüşün de dalgalı ve sınırlı kaldığını belirterek, "Faizlerin yüksekliğinin yanı sıra üyelerimizden bankaların kredilerde uyguladığı komisyon ve dosya masraflarının finansman maliyetlerini ciddi ölçüde artırdığı yönünde bildirimler alıyoruz" açıklamasını yaptı.
Merkez Bankasının 11 Kasım'da KOBİ kredilerinde büyüme sınırını yüzde 5'ten 5,5'e yükseltmesini olumlu bir gelişme olarak değerlendiren Avdagiç, şunları kaydetti:
"Bununla birlikte, mevcut koşullarda bu artışın daha ileri taşınmasının reel sektöre önemli katkı sağlayacağına inanıyoruz. İTO olarak üyelerimiz adına sıklıkla dile getirdiğimiz üzere, KOBİ kredilerindeki büyüme sınırının daha anlamlı ölçüde genişletilmesi ve üretim, ihracat ve yatırım kredilerinin bu sınırın dışında tutulması finansmana erişimi kolaylaştıracaktır. İş dünyamızın 2027'ye uygun finansman koşullarıyla girmesinin üretim, istihdam ve yatırım açısından önemli kazanımlar sağlayacağına inanıyoruz."

15 Temmuz hain darbe girişiminde Türkiye'nin bağımsızlığı ve milli iradesi için canlarını feda eden kahramanların aileleri, Antalya 'da düzenlenen 10. Şehit Aileleri Buluşması'nda bir araya geldi. 15 Temmuz Derneği tarafından gerçekleştirilen programda şehit yakınları, aradan geçen yıllara rağmen taşıdıkları acıyı, gururu ve vatan sevgisini Sabah'tan Barış Savaş'la paylaştı.
"Hep Sen Varsın Diye" temasıyla gerçekleştirilen buluşmada, şehit aileleri arasındaki dayanışma ve kardeşlik ruhu ön plana çıktı. Etkinliğe katılan İçişleri Bakan Yardımcısı Bülent Turan da ailelerle sohbet ederek şehit yakınları ve gazilerle bir arada olmaktan onur duyduğunu ifade etti.
15 Temmuz Derneği'nin şehit yakınlarını yalnız bırakmamak ve darbe girişimini unutturmamak amacıyla yürüttüğü çalışmalara dikkat çeken Bülent Turan, darbeciler ile demokrasi ve milletin yanında duranlar arasında net bir tercih bulunduğunu söyledi.
Turan, "Ya darbecinin yanındasınız ya da demokrasinin, milletin yanındasınız. Ama o darbeciler o hastalığı aldığı zaman kanser hücresi gibi ne zaman fırsat bulsalar bir yerden patlıyor, kendini gösteriyor" ifadelerini kullandı.
Şehitlerin milli iradenin ve demokrasinin korunması için büyük bedel ödediğini vurgulayan Turan, "Evlatlarınız bu ülkede milli irade devam etsin diye, sistem, demokrasi çalışsın diye bedel ödedi. Tekrar tekrar darbe çığırtkanlığı yapmanın bu ülkeye hiçbir faydası yok. Hiçbir darbeden sonra ekonomimizin büyümediğini, siyasetin büyümediğini, ülkemizin büyümediğini yaşayarak gördük. O yüzden demokrasi içerisinde, milli iradenin hakimiyetinde yolumuza devam edeceğiz" dedi.
Toplumsal huzur ve kardeşliğin korunmasının önemine de değinen Turan, "Ne olursa olsun umutsuz olmayacağız. Ne olursa olsun sorunlarımızı aşacağımıza, 86 milyonun kardeşliğiyle beraber aşacağımıza inanarak yola devam edeceğiz" diye konuştu.
15 Temmuz Derneği Başkanı İsmail Hakkı Turunç, yaptığı açıklamada darbe girişiminin uluslararası alanda anlatılması için yürüttükleri çalışmaları anlattı.
Dışişleri Bakanlığı, TİKA, Türkiye Maarif Vakfı ve Yunus Emre Enstitüsü ile ortak programlar gerçekleştirdiklerini belirten Turunç, bugüne kadar 61 ülkeyi ziyaret ederek 15 Temmuz'un perde arkasını anlattıklarını söyledi. Şehit ve gazi çocuklarına yönelik eğitim ve istihdam desteklerinin sürdüğünü de aktaran Turunç, şehit aileleri arasındaki güçlü dayanışmaya dikkat çekti.
Turunç, "Şehit ailelerinin çoğu zaman maddi bir talepten ziyade hatırlanmaya ihtiyacı var. Bir şehit babasını başka bir şehit babası can kulağıyla dinler. Bir şehit annesi başka bir şehit annesini yüzündeki tebessümden, ses tonundan anlar. Aralarında çok güçlü bir kardeşlik ruhu oluştu" ifadelerini kullandı.
15 Temmuz darbe girişiminin başarılı olması halinde Türkiye'nin büyük bir iç savaşa sürükleneceğini belirten Turunç, Başkan Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'ın kararlı tutumu ve milletin meydanlara inmesiyle emperyal planların bozulduğunu kaydetti. Turunç, milli direnişin 11'inci yılında şehit ailelerini kutsal topraklara götürmek için çalışmalar yürüttüklerini de bildirdi.
15 Temmuz gecesi darbe girişiminin seyrini değiştiren kahraman Astsubay Ömer Halisdemir 'in ailesi de buluşmada gurur dolu anlar yaşadı. Şehidin kızı Teğmen Elif Nur Halisdemir, babasının izinden giderek Özel Kuvvetler Komutanlığı bünyesinde bordo bereli oldu.
Şehidin babası Hasan Hüseyin Halisdemir, torununun asker olmasından duyduğu mutluluğu dile getirirken vatan sevgisini şu sözlerle anlattı:
"Üç tane oğlum kaldı. Torunlarım, Ömerlerim var, onları da yetiştiriyorum. Onları da vatana hibe ederim."
Ömer Halisdemir'in kardeşi Soner Halisdemir, ağabeyinin mirasının yeni nesiller tarafından yaşatıldığını belirtti. Şehidin naaşı baba ocağına geldiğinde bordo beresini kızının aldığını ve giydiğini anlatan Soner Halisdemir, yeğeninin bugün de babasının izinden yürüdüğünü söyledi.
Soner Halisdemir, "Bugün Ömer olur, yarın Fatih olur, yarın Ali olur. Bizde Ömerler hiç bitmez. Söz konusu vatan ve milletse 30 kurşun olsa ne yazar, 30 bin kurşun olsa ne yazar? Biz unutmadık, unutturmayacağız" dedi.
Ankara Gölbaşı Özel Harekat Daire Başkanlığı'na düzenlenen saldırıda ikiz polis memuru oğulları Ahmet ve Mehmet Oruç'u şehit veren baba Hacı Ali Oruç da yaşadıklarını paylaştı.
Henüz stajyer olan ve görevleri resmen başlamayan oğullarının, amirlerinin "Gelmeyin" uyarısına rağmen 15 Temmuz gecesi mücadeleye katıldığını anlatan Oruç, ikizlerin "Biz de bu personelin içindeyiz, elimizden geldiği kadar yardımcı olmak istiyoruz" diyerek görev yerlerine gittiklerini aktardı.
Oğullarının helikopterleri hangardan çıkarırken atılan ilk bombayla şehit düştüğünü belirten Hacı Ali Oruç, acı haberi sabah saatlerinde önce Ahmet'in, ardından Mehmet'in şehadetiyle aldığını söyledi.
İki evladını aynı gece kaybeden baba, yaşadığı büyük acıya rağmen gururunu şu sözlerle dile getirdi:
"İki evlat vermek kolay değil; acısı da büyük, makamı da büyük. Cenab-ı Allah bizi bu makama layık gördüyse ne mutlu bize. Her babaya, her anneye nasip olmaz. Oğullarımızla gururlanıyoruz."
15 Temmuz gecesi Türkiye'nin bağımsızlığı için mücadele edenler arasında Türk vatandaşlarının yanı sıra Türkiye'ye gönül veren yabancılar da yer aldı. İstanbul'da çalışan Fas uyruklu Cevad Merrun, Başkan Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'ın çağrısını televizyondan duyduktan sonra arkadaşlarının "Sen misafirimizsin, dışarı çıkma" uyarılarına rağmen sokağa çıktı. Türkiye için tankların karşısına dikilen Merrun, darbe girişimi sırasında şehit düştü.
Ağabeyinin şehadet haberini sabah saat 06.00'da aldıklarını anlatan Selahaddin Merrun, yaşadıkları acıyı ve gururu şu sözlerle aktardı:
"İlk aldığımız haberle yıkıldık ama şehit olduğunu öğrenince büyük bir gurur duyduk. Ağabeyim Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'ı ve Türkiye'yi çok seviyordu. Aradan yıllar geçse de onu hiç aklımdan çıkaramıyorum. Ağabeyimle çok gurur duyuyorum."

Bu yıl 10'uncusu düzenlenen Geleneksel Şehit Aileleri Buluşması, Antalya'nın Kemer ilçesindeki bir otelde gerçekleşti. Geceye Gençlik ve Spor Bakan Yardımcısı Enes Eminoğlu, Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakan Yardımcısı Zafer Tarıkdaroğlu, Antalya Valisi Hulusi Şahin, Kemer Kaymakamı Ahmet Solmaz, Kepez Kaymakamı Suat Dervişoğlu, 15 Temmuz Derneği Başkanı İsmail Hakkı Turunç, şehit yakınları ve protokol üyeleri katıldı.
Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakan Yardımcısı Zafer Tarıkdaroğlu, aynı çatı altında, aynı gönül bağı ile bir araya gelmenin mutluluğunu yaşadıklarını belirterek, 15 Temmuz gecesinde gösterilen iradenin ülkenin kaderini yeniden yazdığını söyledi.
Tarıkdaroğlu, "15 Temmuz gecesi aziz milletimizin demokrasisine, bağımsızlığına ve geleceğine nasıl sahip çıktığını tüm dünyaya göstermiş olduğu bir gecedir. O gece kadın erkek, genç yaşlı demeden meydanlara koşan milletimiz tankların, topların, mermilerin karşısında imanıyla, cesaretiyle ve vatan aşkıyla dimdik durmuştur. O gece ortaya konulan o eşsiz duruş yalnızca bir darbe girişiminin bertaraf edilmesi değil, aynı zamanda bu topraklarda esaretin asla kabul edilmeyeceğinin, milli iradenin üstünde hiçbir gücün bulunmayacağının en gür sesidir. Sizler her daim başımızın tacı, gözümüzün nurusunuz" dedi.
Gençlik ve Spor Bakan Yardımcısı Enes Eminoğlu, 253 şehidi rahmetle, minnetle andıklarını belirterek, bu milletin 1071 Malazgirt Savaşı'nda nasıl düşmana karşı çıktıysa, 15 Temmuz'da da ayrı iradeyle tanklara, uçaklara karşı çıktığını söyledi.
"Asırlık Gece" adlı yapım, Doç. Dr. Hüseyin Aydın’ın “Asırlık Gece” kitabından yola çıkılarak hazırlandı.
Vali Hulusi Şahin, şehit ailelerinin millet için taşıdığı değere vurgu yaparak, "Sizler bizim için çok değerlisiniz. Sizleri ailemizin bir ferdi olarak görüyoruz. Bu toplum, evlatlarını vatanı ve memleketi için gerektiğinde canını feda etmeye hazır olacak şekilde yetiştiriyor" dedi.
Şehit annelerinin vatan sevgisi ve fedakarlığının milletin gücünü ortaya koyduğunu ifade eden Vali Şahin, bir şehit annesinin, "Gerekirse, kaç çocuğum varsa o kadar çocuğumu vatan uğruna veririm" sözüne dikkat çekerek, "Bu millet yıkılmaz, bu millet yılmaz. Böyle analar olduğu müddetçe bu milletin başına hiçbir şey gelmez" diye konuştu.
Rüzgar Aksoy, "Asırlık Gece" filminde 15 Temmuz şehidi Astsubay Kıdemli Başçavuş Ömer Halisdemir’i canlandırdı.
“BU KADAR KAHRAMANA SAHİP BİR KİTLENİN İÇİNDE OLMAK GURUR VERİCİ”
“Asırlık Gece” filminde rol alan oyunculardan Rüzgar Aksoy, 10'uncu Şehit Aileleri Buluşması'na katıldığında şehit yakınları ve gazileri gördüğünde çok duygusal anlar yaşadığını belirtti.
15 Temmuz darbe girişiminin üzerinden 10 yıl geçtiğini belirten Rüzgar Aksoy, "Fakat hala insanların yüzleri gülse de gözlerinin derinliğinde kalp kırıklıklarını görüyorsunuz. Benim için gerçekten bu kadar kahramana sahip bir kitlenin içinde olmak gurur verici" dedi.
